stories.title: RBI's July bulletin shows India's economy holding steady on stronger FDI, FPI, and a surprise current-account surplus
stories.what_happened: The RBI's July 2026 bulletin reported that **strong industrial activity, a healthy services sector, rising exports, and improving foreign investment** have kept India's economy resilient even as many other countries face headwinds. **FDI in April–May 2026 came in higher** than the same two months last year, and **FPI — money foreign investors put into Indian stocks and bonds — turned positive in June and stayed positive in July**, reversing earlier outflows. India's **current account recorded a $4.7 billion surplus in April 2026**, a sharp reversal from a $4.8 billion deficit a year earlier, driven by **net services exports strengthening to $18.6 billion** and **remittances surging to $16 billion** from $9.4 billion. Separately, the RBI **temporarily removed the interest-rate ceiling on foreign-currency (FCNR-B) deposits** with 3–5 year tenors, effective through September 30, giving banks more room to attract NRI deposits.
key_points: RBI's July bulletin says **strong industrial activity and exports** are keeping India's economy on a steady path
**Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in April–May 2026 was higher than the same period last year
**Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI)** turned positive in June and stayed positive through July
India posted a **$4.7 billion current-account surplus** in April, reversing a **$4.8 billion deficit** a year earlier
RBI temporarily lifted the interest-rate ceiling on 3–5 year **NRI foreign-currency deposits** through September 30

depth.background: India's economy has been sending mixed signals lately — a weak monsoon and global trade shocks (including new US tariffs) have weighed on some indicators even as underlying growth held up. The Reserve Bank of India, the country's central bank, publishes a monthly bulletin assessing the state of the economy, and its July edition paints a notably more resilient picture: rising investment inflows and a swing back to a current-account surplus, a sign the country is earning more from trade, services, and remittances than it's spending abroad.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi and Congress escalate pressure on Amit Shah in Rajya Sabha over student 'lathi-charge' claim
stories.what_happened: The confrontation moved to the **Rajya Sabha** on Thursday as the same Public Examinations Amendment Bill was tabled there a day after clearing the Lok Sabha. Congress's deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha, **Pramod Tiwari**, told the House that **'students were lathi-charged, pellet fire used'** during the July 20 protest and that Home Minister Amit Shah, as the constitutionally accountable minister under **Article 75**, must personally answer for it. Separately, Rahul Gandhi told reporters he personally witnessed Shah **'calling the police'** during the protest, and asked **'Why is Amit Shah so scared of coming to Parliament?'**, saying his absence from the debate 'reeks of guilt.' The government has not issued a fresh on-record rebuttal to Thursday's remarks beyond its Wednesday denial that any shots were fired.
key_points: Congress's **Pramod Tiwari** told the Rajya Sabha students were **'lathi-charged, pellet fire used'** and Shah must answer
Rahul Gandhi asked why **Amit Shah is 'so scared' of Parliament**, saying his absence 'reeks of guilt'
Tiwari invoked **Article 75** of the Constitution to argue Shah is directly accountable to the House
The clash came as the **Public Examinations Amendment Bill** was tabled in the Rajya Sabha a day after Lok Sabha passage
It's the same **July 20 student-protest** episode Gandhi raised in the Lok Sabha two days ago

depth.background: On Wednesday, Rahul Gandhi told the Lok Sabha that Home Minister Amit Shah had personally ordered police to fire on students protesting near Jantar Mantar on July 20, calling it a 'shooting' of students and saying police put 'pellets into the blood' of protesters. The government flatly denied it, with ministers saying only tear gas was used and demanding Gandhi apologize for what they called a breach of parliamentary privilege. The clash overshadowed passage of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, itself a response to this year's NEET-UG paper-leak protests.

thread.previously: We reported that Gandhi accused Shah of ordering police to fire on students and use pellets during a July 20 protest, which the government denied, saying only tear gas was used, and demanded Gandhi apologise for a breach of privilege.
thread.changed: The clash moved from the Lok Sabha to the Rajya Sabha, where Congress's Pramod Tiwari cited Article 75 to demand Shah personally answer, and Gandhi publicly asked why Shah is 'scared' to face Parliament.

stories.title: Zaheer Abbas backs Kohli and Rohit for the 2027 World Cup, but tells Rohit to sharpen his fitness
stories.what_happened: Pakistan batting great **Zaheer Abbas** has publicly backed both **Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli** to play the 2027 ODI World Cup, saying **'age should not be a factor as long as they are fit and continue scoring runs.'** On fitness specifically, he said **'Kohli is still supremely fit, while Rohit just needs to pay a little more attention to his fitness.'** The comments follow a strong recent ODI series for India in England, where **Rohit scored his maiden ODI century at Lord's** in the series-deciding final match and **Kohli struck twin fifties**. Both players are next set to feature together in a **home ODI series against the West Indies starting in September**.
key_points: Former Pakistan captain **Zaheer Abbas** says age 'should not be a factor' for Kohli and Rohit at the **2027 ODI World Cup**
He said **Kohli is 'still supremely fit'**, while **Rohit needs to pay more attention to fitness**
Comes after both scored heavily in India's recent **ODI series against England**, including Rohit's maiden Lord's ODI century
The pair next play together in a home ODI series against the **West Indies starting in September**
It contrasts with earlier comments from **Sourav Ganguly**, who said neither is a certainty for 2027

depth.background: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, two of India's most decorated batters, have faced persistent questions about their long-term futures in ODI cricket as they approach their late 30s, with selectors and former players publicly split on whether they should be automatic picks for the 2027 ODI World Cup, to be co-hosted in Africa. Former India captain Sourav Ganguly recently said publicly that neither man's spot should be considered guaranteed.

stories.title: CSK re-emerges as front-runner for Hardik Pandya as IPL's biggest trade saga drags on
stories.what_happened: The trade saga has swung back toward Chennai: multiple reports now describe **CSK as the leading candidate** to land Pandya, offering a deal centred on **Shivam Dube plus additional cash**, rather than including Ayush Mhatre as MI originally wanted. Mumbai's demand for Mhatre alongside Dube remains a sticking point, and CSK is holding firm in refusing to include the young batter. The rival bid from **Delhi Capitals** (Axar Patel and Prithvi Shaw) — which had appeared to gain ground in recent days — seems to have lost momentum as CSK re-asserts itself as the front-runner. As with every stage of this saga, **no franchise has made an official statement**, and all reporting remains speculative.
key_points: Reports now say **Chennai Super Kings is 'emerging as the leading candidate'** to sign Hardik Pandya
CSK is offering a **cash-plus-one-player** package built around **Shivam Dube**
Mumbai Indians still want **Shivam Dube and Ayush Mhatre**; CSK continues to **refuse to include Mhatre**
**Delhi Capitals'** rival offer of Axar Patel and Prithvi Shaw appears to have lost momentum
None of the trade talk has been **officially confirmed** by any of the three franchises involved

depth.background: Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings have been in advanced, unconfirmed talks for weeks over trading MI captain Hardik Pandya to CSK. MI's original ask was Shivam Dube and rising batter Ayush Mhatre; CSK refused to part with Mhatre and countered with Dube, South African batter Dewald Brevis, and roughly ₹10 crore in cash. When that stalled, Delhi Capitals entered the picture offering captain Axar Patel and opener Prithvi Shaw, with Kolkata Knight Riders floated as a fallback if the MI-CSK deal collapsed entirely.

thread.previously: We reported Delhi Capitals had entered the Pandya trade race with an Axar Patel-Prithvi Shaw offer after MI and CSK stalled over CSK's refusal to include Ayush Mhatre, with Kolkata Knight Riders floated as a fallback.
thread.changed: Momentum has swung back to Chennai, with CSK now reported as the leading candidate on a cash-plus-Dube package, while Delhi's rival offer appears to have cooled.

stories.title: Oscar Piastri says he's staying at McLaren for 2027, brushing off Verstappen swap rumours
stories.what_happened: Speaking ahead of the **Belgian Grand Prix**, Piastri was asked directly whether he'd still be driving for McLaren in 2027 and replied simply, **'Yes.'** He added: **'I'm very happy with where I am and where I sit,'** and credited team principal **Andrea Stella** and CEO **Zak Brown** for being 'great' and 'reassuring' amid the swirl of Verstappen-to-McLaren speculation. It follows a rocky Hungarian Grand Prix weekend for Piastri, where he retired from the race with a late gearbox failure after an on-air radio outburst about the team's strategy; McLaren has since said it understands his frustration but stands by the pit call it made.
key_points: Piastri confirmed **'Yes'** when asked directly if he'll race for McLaren in **2027**
He said he's **'very happy'** with his position and praised team principal **Andrea Stella** and CEO **Zak Brown**
The comments respond directly to swirling rumours of a **Verstappen-Piastri driver swap**
Came ahead of the **Belgian Grand Prix**, after Piastri retired from Hungary with a late gearbox failure
McLaren says it understood his frustrated **radio outburst** in Hungary but stands by its pit strategy

depth.background: Speculation has intensified for weeks that Max Verstappen could leave Red Bull for McLaren, with some reports suggesting a swap that could push Piastri out or to another seat, even though Piastri currently sits in McLaren's title fight alongside Lando Norris. Piastri had a difficult Hungarian Grand Prix, retiring with a late gearbox failure and venting frustration over the team's pit strategy on team radio, which added fuel to questions about his long-term standing at McLaren.

stories.title: Red Bull offers Verstappen a contract through 2029 with the exit clause removed — and a bigger paycheck
stories.what_happened: Red Bull has put a new contract offer on the table for Verstappen that would run through the **end of 2029** and, notably, **removes the performance-linked exit clause** that let him leave early under the current deal. The offer also comes with an increased base salary, reportedly rising from roughly **€65 million (£55m)**. Verstappen has **not made an imminent decision** and, according to reports, has until **October** to decide. He remains on F1's summer break, recently photographed on holiday in **Sardinia alongside Mercedes boss Toto Wolff and his wife Susie** — fuel for speculation in both directions, even as Verstappen has taken **three podiums in his last four races**, including second in Hungary despite being openly critical of the car.
key_points: Red Bull's new offer runs through **end of 2029** with **no performance-based exit clause**
Verstappen's base salary would rise from around **€65 million (£55m)**
He has **until October** to decide whether to sign
He's taken **three podiums in the last four races**, including 2nd in Hungary despite criticizing the car
Verstappen was seen on **holiday in Sardinia** with Toto and Susie Wolff, fueling speculation either way

depth.background: Verstappen's current Red Bull contract has an exit clause tied to performance, which has fueled a year of speculation about whether the four-time champion could leave — with Mercedes' Toto Wolff repeatedly declining to fully rule out a future pairing with Verstappen. Red Bull has struggled to match the pace of rivals under F1's new regulations this season, adding to questions about whether Verstappen would stay.

thread.previously: We reported Red Bull wanted to extend Verstappen through 2029 even as his current contract's performance-based exit clause left the door open for him to leave.
thread.changed: Red Bull has now made a concrete offer that removes that exit clause entirely and raises his salary, with Verstappen given until October to decide.

stories.title: Microsoft's cloud business beats forecasts as Meta's AI spending still shows no clear payoff
stories.what_happened: Microsoft reported fiscal fourth-quarter results after Wednesday's close, showing Azure cloud revenue grew **43% year-over-year** — the fastest pace since early 2022 — comfortably beating the roughly 40% growth Wall Street had priced in, with Azure's full fiscal-year revenue topping **$100 billion** for the first time. Meta reported the same evening; analysts had expected revenue to rise about 27% to roughly $60 billion and earnings per share of about $7.18, driven mainly by steady ad growth, but Meta's forecast for the next quarter came in **lackluster**, disappointing investors hoping for proof its enormous AI infrastructure spending would show up somewhere beyond the ad business. The contrast — one hyperscaler with a concrete, fast-growing AI-linked revenue stream, the other still mostly promising future payoff — helped **lift US stock futures and Asian markets** in early trading after two days of heavy selling tied to the Fed decision and the chip-stock rout.
key_points: Microsoft's Azure cloud revenue jumped **43% year-over-year**, its fastest growth since early 2022, beating Wall Street's ~40% estimate.
Azure's full fiscal-year revenue crossed **$100 billion** for the first time.
Meta reported the same day but has **no cloud business of its own** to point to as proof its AI spending is paying off outside advertising.
The divergent reports landed right after the Fed's rate hold and a **$1 trillion+ Asian chip-stock rout** revived doubts about the AI trade.
Microsoft's beat helped **lift US and Asian stock futures** in early trading after two days of selling.

depth.background: Over the past two years, Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Meta have collectively spent hundreds of billions of dollars building **AI data centers** and buying chips, betting that AI will eventually generate outsized revenue. Wall Street has grown anxious about whether that spending is paying off, especially after a rough week in which the Fed held interest rates and a memory-chip selloff triggered by South Korea's SK Hynix wiped out over **$1 trillion** in chipmaker value. Microsoft's cloud division, Azure, rents out computing power — including AI capacity — to other companies, making its revenue one of the clearest read-outs of whether AI demand is real. Meta, by contrast, mostly sells AI-boosted advertising and has no comparable business to show investors as separate proof.

stories.title: India's Commonwealth Games medal count climbs into double digits, led by Mirabai Chanu's historic hat-trick gold
stories.what_happened: As of Thursday, India's medal tally at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games stood at **12** — 2 gold, 7 silver and 3 bronze — good for 9th place overall. The headline result came from weightlifter **Mirabai Chanu**, who won gold in the women's 48kg category with a total lift of **190kg** (an 85kg snatch and 105kg clean & jerk), breaking the Games record in all three categories and completing her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold after Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022. Other medals have come from weightlifters Chanambam Rishikanta Singh, Raja Muthupandi and Valluri Ajaya Babu (silvers) and Bindyarani Devi Sorokhaibam (bronze), plus silvers from high jumper Sarvesh Kushare and long jumper **Murali Sreeshankar**, who became the first Indian man with two Commonwealth Games medals in that event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been publicly congratulating each medalist as results come in. India's campaign continues Thursday with javelin star **Neeraj Chopra** beginning his qualifying round, and shot putters Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Samardeep Singh Gill contesting the final, alongside weightlifting finals in the heavier categories.
key_points: India's medal tally at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games has reached **12 medals** — 2 gold, 7 silver, 3 bronze — placing it **9th** on the table.
Weightlifter **Mirabai Chanu** delivered a **third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold**, breaking Games records in the snatch, clean & jerk and total (190kg) in the women's 48kg category.
Silvers have come from **Sarvesh Kushare** (high jump) and **Murali Sreeshankar** (long jump, his second CWG medal), plus three weightlifters.
**PM Modi** has been publicly congratulating each medalist as the tally builds.
Thursday brings more chances: **Neeraj Chopra** opens his javelin title defense and **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** goes into the shot put final.

depth.background: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are being held in **Glasgow, Scotland**, from July 23 to August 2 — the same city that hosted the 2014 Games, where a young Mirabai Chanu won her first CWG medal, a silver. She has won a medal at every Commonwealth Games since, culminating in Thursday's historic third straight gold. India has traditionally been strongest at these Games in weightlifting, wrestling, badminton and athletics, and this edition is following that pattern, with weightlifting supplying most of the country's medals in the opening week.

stories.title: India and China's readout from the Beijing visit: both sides commit to peace on the disputed border
stories.what_happened: India's **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** released its official readout of Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's two-day Beijing visit, confirming that both India and China **reaffirmed the importance of maintaining peace and tranquility along the LAC** — an explicit, mutual commitment on the border question that goes beyond the general 'partners not rivals' language reported when the visit first concluded. The MEA said Misri held **wide-ranging discussions** covering trade, cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges, and political engagement. Separate from his earlier meetings with Vice Foreign Minister **Hua Chunying** and Communist Party official **Sun Haiyan**, Misri also met **Li Wentang**, Vice President of the Communist Party's **Central Party School**, receiving a briefing on the institution's role and discussing future academic and policy exchanges between the two countries.
key_points: India and China **reaffirmed maintaining peace along the LAC** (Line of Actual Control), the disputed Himalayan border.
The commitment came in the **official readout** from Foreign Secretary **Vikram Misri's** two-day Beijing visit.
Misri also met **Li Wentang**, Vice President of the Communist Party's **Central Party School**, to discuss future cooperation.
The talks build on efforts to implement an understanding reached between **PM Modi and President Xi Jinping**.
It follows Misri's earlier meetings with Vice Foreign Minister **Hua Chunying** and party official **Sun Haiyan**.

depth.background: India and China share a long, disputed Himalayan border called the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** — there is no final, mutually agreed border line, which is why troop clashes (like the deadly 2020 Galwan Valley confrontation) have periodically flared. Since then, the two countries have been on a slow path toward normalizing ties: restoring some direct flights, easing visa rules, and resuming senior diplomatic visits, even as the underlying border dispute remains unresolved. **Vikram Misri**, India's Foreign Secretary, is the top career diplomat managing this delicate reset.

thread.previously: We reported that Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri concluded a two-day Beijing visit on July 29, meeting China's Vice Foreign Minister Hua Chunying and a Communist Party official, with both sides talking about framing each other as 'partners' rather than rivals — but without a concrete outcome beyond the tone of the talks.
thread.changed: The official Indian government readout now confirms a specific, substantive commitment: both sides reaffirmed the importance of maintaining peace and tranquility along the disputed Line of Actual Control (LAC), and Misri held an additional meeting with Li Wentang of the Communist Party's Central Party School — details not available when the visit merely 'wrapped up.'

stories.title: India's Jaismine Lamboria reaches Commonwealth Games boxing semi-final, guarantees the country's 10th medal in Glasgow
stories.what_happened: On Wednesday in Glasgow, Lamboria defeated England's Elise Glynn by a **4-1 split decision** in the women's 57kg quarter-final, producing a strong final round to seal the win. The victory guarantees her at least a **bronze medal**, taking India's medal tally at the 2026 Commonwealth Games to **10**. She will fight Lesotho's Rapelang Maselela in the semi-final on **Friday**; a win there would send her into the gold-medal match and guarantee at least a silver. This is Lamboria's second consecutive Commonwealth Games medal, having also won bronze at Birmingham 2022, and comes on the back of her 2025 World Boxing Championships gold in the same weight category.
key_points: Lamboria beat England's Elise Glynn **4-1** in the women's 57kg quarter-final in Glasgow
The result guarantees India **at least a bronze** — its **10th medal** of the 2026 Commonwealth Games
She's the reigning **world champion** in the 57kg category, having won gold at the 2025 World Boxing Championships
It's her **second straight Commonwealth Games medal**, after bronze at Birmingham 2022
She faces Lesotho's Rapelang Maselela in the semi-final on **Friday**, with a win putting her in the gold-medal bout

depth.background: The **Commonwealth Games** is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from Commonwealth nations (mostly former British territories), roughly comparable in prestige to a smaller Olympics. India has traditionally been strong in boxing at the Games. **Jaismine Lamboria**, from Haryana, is one of India's rising stars in the sport — she won the world title in her weight class in 2025 and had already medaled at the previous Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in 2022.

stories.title: A divided Fed holds interest rates steady for a fifth straight meeting — and three officials openly revolt
stories.what_happened: The Federal Open Market Committee voted **9-3** on July 29 to leave the federal funds rate unchanged in a range of **3.50% to 3.75%**, the fifth consecutive meeting without a change. Three regional Fed presidents — Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis) and Lorie Logan (Dallas) — dissented, all arguing rates should have gone **up**, not stayed flat. That is the first time since **September 2016** that three policymakers have dissented in the same direction. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters afterward that the central bank has **'no soft inflation target'** and will act if prices keep climbing, a notably hawkish signal. The decision came the same week the government reported US GDP grew just 1.5% in the second quarter, undershooting forecasts, showing the Fed is torn between a economy that's cooling and inflation that isn't.
key_points: The Fed kept its key rate at **3.50%–3.75%** for the **fifth meeting in a row**.
Three regional bank presidents **dissented**, wanting a hike instead — the first three-way split like this since **2016**.
Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** said there's 'no soft inflation target' and the Fed won't hesitate to act.
The split reflects a real fight inside the Fed over whether **tariff-driven inflation** is temporary or sticking around.
Markets had priced in a possible rate cut by September — this dissent makes that **less certain**.

depth.background: The US Federal Reserve sets the country's benchmark interest rate — the cost of borrowing money — through its rate-setting committee, the **FOMC**, which meets roughly every six weeks. Central banks raise rates to cool inflation (making borrowing pricier slows spending) and cut them to boost a weak economy. The Fed has held rates flat since earlier this year as it weighs two conflicting pressures: **inflation that Trump's tariffs have kept elevated**, and a labor market that has been quietly slowing. Kevin Warsh became Fed Chair this year and has taken a notably hawkish (inflation-focused) public tone compared to his predecessor.

stories.title: The Fed holds rates steady at 3.50%-3.75%, but three officials dissent wanting hikes
stories.what_happened: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) met on July 28-29, 2026 and voted **9-3** to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at **3.50%-3.75%**. Three regional Fed bank presidents — Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari, and Dallas's Lorie Logan — broke ranks and voted for a **rate hike instead**, arguing that five-plus years of above-target inflation demands more forceful action. The Fed's statement acknowledged 'elevated uncertainty' tied to the ongoing Middle East conflict, but noted the broader economy is 'expanding at a solid pace,' with strong productivity growth, solid capital investment, and a stable unemployment rate. Markets, which had been betting on rate cuts, are now pricing in two 25-basis-point **hikes** by year-end.
key_points: The Fed's rate-setting committee voted **9-3** to hold the federal funds rate at **3.50%-3.75%**.
Three regional Fed presidents **dissented in favor of raising rates**, an unusually large revolt.
Their reason: **inflation has stayed above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years**.
The Fed cited **elevated uncertainty from the Middle East conflict** but said the economy is 'expanding at a solid pace'.
Markets now price **two 25-basis-point hikes**, in September and December, not the cuts many expected.

depth.background: The Federal Reserve is the US **central bank** — it sets the interest rate at which banks lend to each other overnight, which ripples out into mortgage rates, credit card rates, and business borrowing costs everywhere. Since 2021, US **inflation** (the pace at which prices rise) has run hotter than the Fed's 2% comfort zone almost continuously, partly fueled by pandemic-era spending, supply shocks, and now Middle East war-driven oil price spikes. The Fed's job is to balance cooling inflation against not choking off growth or jobs — a trade-off that gets harder when a war is adding a fresh, unpredictable inflation shock on top of an already-sticky problem.

stories.title: India launches 'SHANTI' campaign for a UN Security Council seat, keeping its bigger ask alive
stories.what_happened: Jaishankar unveiled the 'SHANTI' campaign — Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity — at the UN in New York, formally launching India's bid for a non-permanent UNSC seat covering **2028-29**. The campaign's platform centers on peacekeeping, counter-terrorism, maritime security, climate action, sustainable development, and amplifying the voice of the 'Global South' (developing nations). The actual election for the seat happens in **June 2027**, and India will be competing against **Tajikistan** for the single vacancy allotted to the Asia-Pacific regional group. Indian officials were explicit that this campaign complements — not replaces — India's decades-long demand for a **permanent** seat with veto power.
key_points: External Affairs Minister **S. Jaishankar** unveiled India's 'SHANTI' campaign at UN headquarters in New York.
SHANTI stands for **'Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.'**
It's a bid for a **non-permanent** UNSC seat for **2028-29**, with the election in **June 2027**.
India will compete against **Tajikistan** for the single Asia-Pacific seat available.
The campaign is explicitly framed as reinforcing India's long-standing push for a **permanent** UNSC seat.

depth.background: The UN Security Council is the UN's most powerful body — it can authorize sanctions, peacekeeping missions, and military action. It has **5 permanent members with veto power** (US, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms. India has long argued the permanent-member list is outdated — frozen since 1945 — and doesn't reflect today's world, especially the exclusion of the world's most populous country. Winning non-permanent seats regularly is India's way of staying visible and influential at the UNSC while the much harder fight for permanent membership (which requires a UN Charter change requiring consent from existing permanent members, including a reluctant China) grinds on.

stories.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the fastest-growing on record as the UN names a new crisis coordinator
stories.what_happened: Since our last update, the outbreak's toll has climbed further: confirmed cases have grown from roughly 2,100 to **3,360**, and deaths from about 800 to **1,487**. The United Nations has now appointed **Julien Harneis**, a veteran humanitarian official, to coordinate the international response. Separately, the World Food Programme's acting executive director, **Carl Skau**, visited hard-hit Ituri province and called the situation a **"crisis on top of a crisis"** — the outbreak is compounding a food emergency that already had more than **5 million Congolese** facing emergency-level hunger. Skau also flagged that the **$2.1 billion** humanitarian appeal for Congo is only **45% funded**, leaving responders short of the money needed to fight both crises at once.
key_points: The outbreak has now killed **1,487 people** across **3,360 confirmed cases**, according to the latest tallies.
It took just **over two months** to reach **1,000 deaths** — far faster than the **2014–2016 West Africa outbreak**, which took about **eight months** to hit that toll.
The UN named veteran humanitarian official **Julien Harneis** to coordinate the international response.
The World Food Programme warns the crisis is now **worsening hunger** for over **5 million** already food-insecure people in Ituri province.
The **Bundibugyo strain** driving this outbreak has **no approved vaccine or treatment**, unlike most of Congo's past Ebola outbreaks.

depth.background: This Ebola outbreak, caused by the **Bundibugyo strain** of the virus, has been tearing through eastern DR Congo's conflict-scarred Ituri province for months. We reported yesterday that it had already climbed to the **third-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded**, with a mob attack forcing patients and staff to flee Nyakunde Hospital and UN peacekeepers deploying to protect health workers. Eastern Congo's history of armed-group violence and deep community distrust of outside responders has repeatedly made it harder to isolate patients and trace contacts — the basic tools that stop an outbreak from spreading.

thread.previously: We reported the outbreak had reached roughly 2,100 confirmed cases and 800 deaths, becoming the third-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, after a mob attack forced patients and staff to flee Nyakunde Hospital and UN peacekeepers deployed nearby.
thread.changed: Cases and deaths have climbed sharply (to 3,360 cases and 1,487 deaths), the UN has named a dedicated coordinator, Julien Harneis, and the WFP has issued a new warning that the outbreak is now compounding a severe hunger crisis in the region.

stories.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady with three officials wanting a hike instead — and Wall Street has its worst day of the year
stories.what_happened: The Federal Open Market Committee voted **9-3** on July 29 to hold its benchmark rate at **3.5%–3.75%**, defying expectations that had swung between a possible cut and a hold. The three dissenting officials wanted to **raise** rates instead, arguing inflation risk was being underestimated — a rare and hawkish form of dissent. Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to reining in inflation while calling the economy and labor market 'solid.' Markets read the split vote and Warsh's tone as a sign the Fed is worried about inflation re-accelerating, and **bond yields jumped** on the idea the Fed might be moving too slowly. Stocks sold off sharply: the **Dow dropped 1,153 points (2.19%)** for its worst single day this year, the **S&P 500 fell 1.52%**, and the **Nasdaq Composite lost 1.74%**. The **Nasdaq 100 closed down more than 11% from its June record high**, tipping it into what Wall Street calls a technical correction.
key_points: The Federal Reserve kept its key interest rate at **3.5%–3.75%** in a **9-3 vote** — an unusually split decision.
The three dissenters didn't want a cut, they wanted a **rate hike**, a rare signal of internal alarm over inflation.
The **Dow fell 1,153 points (-2.19%)**, its worst day of the year; the **S&P 500 slid 1.52%**.
The **Nasdaq 100 fell into 'correction' territory** — down more than **11% from its June peak**.
New Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** stressed fighting inflation even as he called the labor market 'solid.'

depth.background: The **Federal Reserve** is the US central bank — it sets the short-term interest rate that ripples through mortgages, credit cards, business loans, and ultimately stock prices worldwide, because the US dollar and US Treasury bonds sit at the center of the global financial system. For most of this year the debate was whether the Fed would **cut** rates to support a cooling economy. **Kevin Warsh**, who recently took over as Fed Chair from Jerome Powell, has positioned himself as an inflation hawk. A 'correction' is Wall Street's term for a **10%+ drop from a recent high** — the line investors watch as a marker of serious, not just noisy, selling.

stories.title: The Fed holds interest rates steady for a fifth straight meeting — but two officials just voted to cut
stories.what_happened: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee voted Wednesday to hold its benchmark federal funds rate in the **4.25%–4.5% range**, marking five consecutive meetings without a change. Two of the Fed's own governors, **Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman**, dissented from the decision, preferring to cut rates by a quarter of a percentage point immediately. The announcement came at 2pm ET after a two-day meeting that began Tuesday, with Fed Chair's press conference following at 2:30pm ET to explain the reasoning and hint at what comes next. Economists had broadly expected the hold, but the size and prominence of the dissent — two sitting governors publicly breaking ranks — is unusual and signals a real internal split over how much longer to wait.
key_points: The Fed kept its benchmark rate at **4.25%–4.5%**, unchanged for a fifth straight meeting
Governors **Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman dissented**, wanting a quarter-point cut now
The decision landed at **2pm ET** Wednesday, with the Chair's press conference to follow
It comes hours after **oil jumped 5%** on the Iran missile strike, muddying the inflation outlook
No new economic projections were released at this meeting, so guidance rests on the press conference

depth.background: The Federal Reserve sets the interest rate that ripples through everything from US mortgages to global capital flows, and it has held that rate roughly flat for months while inflation stays **above its 2% target**. Markets have spent weeks debating whether the Fed would finally start cutting, given a labor market that's held up better than feared even as price pressures linger. A rate decision is normally a single number, but a **dissent** — when one or more of the Fed's own policymakers vote against the majority — is a rare, loud signal about where the debate inside the institution actually stands.

stories.title: Adani Enterprises posts record EBITDA but swings to a net loss after a ₹2,644-crore US sanctions settlement hits the books
stories.what_happened: Adani Enterprises released results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) on India's biggest earnings day of the season. Revenue from operations rose about 50% year-on-year to roughly ₹33,546 crore, and EBITDA hit a record ₹5,642 crore, up 49%. Profit before tax was ₹1,295 crore, roughly flat with a year earlier — but once the ₹2,644 crore exceptional charge from the OFAC settlement is included, the company reported a **net loss attributable to owners of ₹1,160 crore** for the quarter. Segment by segment, Adani Airports' EBITDA rose to about ₹1,633 crore, helped by Navi Mumbai International Airport beginning international operations on July 15; the fledgling copper business added ₹749 crore in EBITDA; and solar module manufacturing capacity grew to 5.7 GW. The company also closed a ₹15,000 crore QIP, with proceeds earmarked mainly for the Adani New Industries ecosystem and finishing the Navi Mumbai airport.
key_points: **Adani Enterprises** reported record **Q1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹5,642 crore**, up **49% year-on-year**, on revenue up roughly **50% to ₹33,546 crore**.

Despite that operating strength, the company posted a **net loss of ₹1,160 crore** after a **₹2,644 crore (~$275 million) charge** tied to a US Treasury (OFAC) Iran-sanctions settlement flowed through this quarter.
**Adani Airports'** EBITDA jumped up to **61% YoY** to ~₹1,633 crore, boosted by **Navi Mumbai International Airport** starting international flights on July 15.
The company completed a **₹15,000 crore Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP)** — one of India's largest infrastructure equity raises this year.
The new **copper business** contributed **₹749 crore** in EBITDA as solar module capacity expanded to **5.7 GW**.

depth.background: Adani Enterprises is the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, India's largest infrastructure conglomerate, which has faced sustained US regulatory scrutiny since a 2024 Department of Justice and SEC bribery indictment. In May 2026, the group separately settled with the US Treasury's **Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)** for **$275 million** over 32 apparent violations of US Iran sanctions — LPG cargo shipments routed through a Dubai trader between November 2023 and June 2025, paid via US dollar transactions. That settlement is now being recognised as a one-time charge in this quarter's results, even though operationally the company's newer businesses — airports, copper, solar — are scaling up fast.

stories.title: McLaren runs Norris, Piastri and F2 champion Fornaroli through a 2-day Portimao test
stories.what_happened: McLaren spent two days at Portimao running Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, and Formula 2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli in a 2023-specification car, completing 49, 55, and 47 laps respectively. Strong afternoon winds added a challenge, with changing gusts affecting car balance through the lap. The test doubled as a scouting and development opportunity for Fornaroli — McLaren's likely young-driver prospect — who got to observe both current McLaren race drivers' driving style and technical feedback firsthand, having traveled straight from Budapest after his second official F1 practice outing. It came just before teams enter F1's mandated summer shutdown period.
key_points: McLaren completed a **2-day private test** at Portimao, Portugal before F1's summer break.
Lando Norris drove **49 laps**, Oscar Piastri **55 laps**, and F2 champion **Leonardo Fornaroli 47 laps**.
The car used was a **2023-spec McLaren** (a 'Testing of Previous Cars' run, the only kind of in-season testing F1 rules allow).
Portimao is set to **return to the F1 calendar in 2027**, making this valuable track-learning time.
Fornaroli got to watch both race drivers' technique and feedback style up close.

depth.background: F1 severely restricts in-season testing to control costs and keep competition fair — teams can't just test their current car whenever they want. The workaround is 'Testing of Previous Cars' (TPC), where teams run an older car (here, a 2023-spec machine) at a circuit, which is allowed because it's not directly developing the current title-fighting car. Portimao, on Portugal's Algarve coast, hosted F1 races in 2020-2021 during the pandemic-shuffled calendar and is confirmed to return in 2027 under the sport's new rules cycle — so track time now is a head start for drivers and teams.

stories.title: Sensex jumps 889 points and Nifty IT surges as Infosys results and the Fed's rate hold lift sentiment
stories.what_happened: The **BSE Sensex gained 888.68 points, or 1.16%,** to close at **77,654.60** on Wednesday, July 29, while the **Nifty 50 advanced 264.85 points, or 1.10%,** to **24,250.20**. The rally was led by technology stocks: the **Nifty IT index jumped roughly 2.3% in the session** and has now climbed **nearly 16% in July alone**, recovering more than 21% from its 52-week low touched on July 1. **Infosys** was the standout, gaining after it posted **9% year-on-year growth in consolidated net profit to ₹6,921 crore** and **8% revenue growth to ₹42,279 crore** for the quarter ended June, with investors also cheering its forward earnings commentary. Banking stocks also firmed, with the Bank Nifty index up 0.79% to 57,205.90. Analysts pointed to a combination of factors: a stronger rupee, foreign institutional investors covering short positions (buying back stock they had bet against), and calmer global sentiment after the **US Federal Reserve's decision a day earlier to hold interest rates steady** rather than signal further tightening.
key_points: The Sensex climbed **888.68 points (1.16%)** to close at **77,654.60**; the Nifty 50 rose **264.85 points (1.10%)** to **24,250.20**.
**Nifty IT jumped over 2.3%** in a single session and is up **nearly 16% for the month of July** — one of the sector's sharpest rallies in years.
**Infosys** led the charge after strong Q1 FY27 results: consolidated net profit rose **9% year-on-year to ₹6,921 crore**, revenue rose **8% to ₹42,279 crore**.
A weaker **rupee-driven currency tailwind** and **FII short-covering** (foreign investors closing bearish bets) added extra fuel to the rally.
The rally came right after the **US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady**, which investors read as reducing near-term global risk.

depth.background: India's stock market runs on two headline indices: the **Sensex** (30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange) and the **Nifty 50** (50 large companies on the National Stock Exchange) — both are 'scoreboards' for how big Indian companies are doing as a group. IT services (companies like Infosys, TCS, and Wipro that sell software and outsourcing services mostly to Western clients) is one of India's largest and most export-driven sectors, so it's highly sensitive to the **rupee's exchange rate** (a weaker rupee means the dollar revenue these firms earn abroad converts into more rupees at home) and to US economic health, since America is their biggest client base. The sector had been in a slump for much of 2026 after a slower spending environment among Western clients, hitting a 52-week low as recently as **July 1**.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha passes bill making it a crime to insult India's national song, Vande Mataram
stories.what_happened: On Wednesday, the **Rajya Sabha** (the upper house of India's Parliament) passed the **Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026** by voice vote, extending the 1971 Act's protections to Vande Mataram for the first time. Under the amended law, anyone who **intentionally prevents or obstructs** the singing of the national song, or who commits a **deliberate act of insult or disrespect** toward it, can face up to **three years in prison** or a fine. The bill was taken up for debate in the post-lunch session, and Opposition MPs — including members of the Congress party and the CPI(M) — objected during the discussion and **walked out** of the House in protest before the vote.
key_points: The **Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026** passed by voice vote in the Rajya Sabha
It extends the same legal protection already given to the **national flag, Constitution, and national anthem** to the national song, Vande Mataram
Deliberately insulting it or obstructing its singing can now bring up to **three years in prison**
The Opposition, led by Congress, **walked out** in protest during the debate
It amends the **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971**

depth.background: **Vande Mataram** ('I Bow to Thee, Mother') is India's national song, distinct from the national anthem (Jana Gana Mana), written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and closely tied to India's independence movement. Since 1971, a law has made it a criminal offence to insult the **national flag**, the **Constitution**, or the **national anthem** — but the national song had never carried the same legal protection. The debate over extending that protection has periodically resurfaced, including around Vande Mataram's 150th anniversary events in late 2025.

stories.title: PM Modi to launch a 100-week anti-drug youth campaign aiming to pledge 1 crore volunteers at 10,000 sites
stories.what_happened: Mandaviya announced that PM Modi will launch the 'Nasha Mukta Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyaan' — roughly, 'Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India Resolve Campaign' — on August 2, 2026. It is designed as a 100-week 'Jan Bhagidari' (public-participation) movement against drug abuse, with simultaneous launch-day events planned at nearly 10,000 locations nationwide. Organisers expect more than 1 crore youth to take a 'Nasha Mukti' (freedom-from-drugs) pledge and sign up as volunteers. The campaign draws on MY Bharat volunteers, NSS cadres, youth clubs, schools, colleges, universities, NGOs, industrial associations and more than 125 spiritual and religious organisations. Weekly activities — walkathons, sports events, meditation sessions, street plays and art competitions — will run every Sunday, with formal recognition milestones marked at weeks 50, 75 and 100 of the campaign.
key_points: PM Modi will launch the **'Nasha Mukta Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyaan'** anti-drug campaign on **August 2**.
It's a **100-week** nationwide movement with simultaneous events planned at nearly **10,000 locations** across India.
Organisers expect more than **1 crore (10 million) youth** to take a drug-free pledge and volunteer as 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Volunteers.'
Participants include **MY Bharat volunteers, NSS cadres**, schools, colleges, NGOs and **over 125 spiritual/religious organisations**.
Weekly Sunday activities — walkathons, sports, meditation, street plays — will run with recognition milestones at **weeks 50, 75 and 100**.

depth.background: The campaign builds on the government's longstanding 'Nasha Mukt Bharat' (drug-free India) messaging and years of state-level anti-drug abhiyaans, but is pitched as the largest and most structured iteration yet. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports **Mansukh Mandaviya** announced the launch details on July 29, ahead of the formal kickoff.

stories.title: Fauci invokes the Fifth Amendment over 100 times at a Senate hearing on Covid's origins, and now faces a contempt vote
stories.what_happened: On **July 29**, Fauci appeared before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee under subpoena from Senator **Rand Paul**. Citing advice from his attorneys, Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination **more than 100 times** rather than answer questions, including from Senator James Lankford about the Covid lab-leak theory. The hearing ran **over two hours** and grew heated, with Fauci calling Paul's pursuit of him an 'unhinged obsession' and saying Paul wants him to say something that could land him 'behind bars.' Paul, who chairs the committee, announced it will vote on a **contempt resolution** against Fauci next week. Democrats on the committee pushed back, defending Fauci's constitutional right to decline to answer and thanking him for his years of government service.
key_points: Fauci pleaded the Fifth **over 100 times** rather than answer questions about the Covid-19 lab-leak theory.
Senator **Rand Paul**, who chairs the committee, says he'll bring a **contempt resolution** against Fauci next week.
Fauci accused Paul of an 'unhinged obsession' aimed at seeing him **jailed**.
Democrats on the committee **defended** Fauci's constitutional right to stay silent.
The hearing lasted **over two hours** and revisited the origins of a pandemic that killed millions.

depth.background: Anthony Fauci ran the US government's top infectious-disease institute for decades and became the public face of America's Covid-19 response in 2020-21. Since then, Republicans in Congress — led by Senator **Rand Paul**, a doctor himself — have accused him of downplaying the possibility that the virus leaked from a Chinese lab and of steering funding toward risky research there. Paul subpoenaed Fauci to testify before the **Senate Homeland Security Committee**, setting up a combative face-off years in the making. The Fifth Amendment gives any American the right to refuse to answer questions that could incriminate them — invoking it is not itself an admission of guilt.

stories.title: Colapinto and Bortoleto grind through a 2,892km Pirelli tyre test in Budapest ahead of F1's 2027 rule reset
stories.what_happened: On Wednesday, Bortoleto and Colapinto took turns in specially prepared test cars at the **Hungaroring** in Budapest, each logging over 500km, for a combined **2,892km** across Audi, Alpine and Aston Martin's entries over two days. The session ran in extreme heat, with track temperatures reaching **59°C**, deliberately stress-testing Pirelli's proposed **C3, C4 and C5** tyre compounds for the 2027 rules for durability and degradation under punishing conditions. Bortoleto set the faster benchmark lap of **1:19.917** versus Colapinto's **1:20.139**, though outright lap time wasn't the point of the exercise — tyre data was.
key_points: Alpine's **Franco Colapinto** and Audi's **Gabriele Bortoleto** completed a punishing **2,892km combined test** in Budapest.
Track temperatures hit a brutal **59°C** during the two-day session.
Bortoleto's best lap of **1:19.917** edged out Colapinto's **1:20.139**.
The test targeted Pirelli's proposed **C3, C4 and C5 compounds** being developed for the **2027 season** — F1's next major rules reset.
Audi, Alpine and Aston Martin combined for **660 laps** across the two days of testing.

depth.background: F1 is preparing a major regulation overhaul for **2027**, covering engines, aerodynamics and tyres. Before any new rules go live, teams and tyre supplier **Pirelli** run extensive private tests to make sure new tyre compounds behave predictably under real race conditions. This kind of testing rarely makes headlines, but it directly shapes how competitive and how safe the 2027 grid will be.

stories.title: Trent Rockets sweep Welsh Fire in a men's and women's Hundred double-header at Cardiff
stories.what_happened: At Sophia Gardens in Cardiff, Trent Rockets swept both matches of a men's-and-women's double-header against Welsh Fire. In the men's game, Welsh Fire were limited to **122 for 7**, and Trent Rockets chased the target down comfortably, reaching **126 for 1** with **Ben Duckett unbeaten on 52**, winning by **9 wickets with 28 balls to spare** — handing Welsh Fire their first defeat of the season. In the women's match, Welsh Fire posted **129 for 3**, but Trent Rockets chased it down by **8 wickets**, powered by **Beth Mooney's 57 off just 35 balls**, to complete the clean sweep for the day.
key_points: Trent Rockets men beat Welsh Fire by **9 wickets**, chasing 123 with **28 balls to spare**
**Ben Duckett** top-scored with an unbeaten **52**; it was Welsh Fire's **first defeat of the season**
In the women's match, Trent Rockets won by **8 wickets**, chasing down Welsh Fire's 129/3
**Beth Mooney** smashed **57 off 35 balls** to seal the women's win
Both matches were played at **Sophia Gardens, Cardiff**, on July 29

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's short-format cricket competition, where each team faces 100 balls per innings (rather than the more familiar 120 balls in a T20 match). It runs men's and women's competitions in parallel, often as double-headers at the same ground on the same day, with eight city-based franchise teams. **Welsh Fire** and **Trent Rockets** are two of those franchises.

stories.title: Tajinderpal Singh Toor qualifies for the Commonwealth Games shot put final, setting up a duel with defending champion Tom Walsh
stories.what_happened: In Wednesday's qualifying round at the **2026 Commonwealth Games** in Glasgow, Toor sealed his spot in the final with a **20.14m** throw on his second attempt, finishing second overall behind Walsh's opening throw of **21.03m**. Fellow Indian competitor Samardeep Singh Gill also progressed through qualifying. Both will now compete in Friday's medal final against Walsh and the rest of the qualified field.
key_points: India's shot put national record holder **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** threw **20.14m** to qualify for Thursday's final.
New Zealand's **Tom Walsh**, the defending Commonwealth Games champion, topped qualifying with a first-round **21.03m**.
Fellow Indian **Samardeep Singh Gill** also advanced to the final.
Toor is chasing his **first-ever Commonwealth Games medal** in the event.
The final takes place **Friday, July 31**.

depth.background: **Tajinderpal Singh Toor** holds the Indian national record in shot put and has been one of India's most consistent throwers for years, but a Commonwealth Games medal in the event has eluded him so far. **Tom Walsh** of New Zealand is the reigning Commonwealth Games champion and one of the most dominant shot putters in the world, making him the clear favorite heading into Friday's final.

stories.title: Barbados holds Sir Garfield Sobers' state funeral at Kensington Oval
stories.what_happened: Following days of public mourning — with Sobers's body lying in state first at Barbados's Parliament on July 27, then at Kensington Oval on July 28 — the island held his official state funeral on Wednesday, July 29, at 10am. The service comprised a public thanksgiving ceremony at Kensington Oval, the ground where he built much of his legend, followed by a private funeral at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens in Christ Church. The government made free public tickets available across the island for those wanting to attend in person, and the ceremony was also livestreamed via the Barbados Parliament's official channel for those who couldn't.
key_points: Barbados held a **state funeral** for Sir Garfield Sobers at Kensington Oval on Wednesday at **10am**
The service included a **public thanksgiving** at the Oval, followed by a **private funeral** at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens
Free public tickets were distributed islandwide, with the service also carried on a **livestream**
Sobers, who died at **89**, lay in state at Parliament on July 27 and at Kensington Oval on July 28
A state funeral is among the **highest honours** Barbados can bestow, reflecting his status as a National Hero

depth.background: Sir Garfield Sobers is widely regarded as the greatest all-rounder in cricket history — a batter, bowler and fielder who redefined what one player could do on a cricket field during his career with the West Indies. He was Barbados's first National Hero to receive this level of state honour tied so directly to his sport, and Kensington Oval is the very ground most associated with his legend, making it the natural site for the public to say goodbye.

thread.previously: We reported Sobers's body was lying in state at Kensington Oval on July 28, ahead of a state funeral confirmed for Wednesday, July 29, at 10am.
thread.changed: That state funeral has now actually taken place — the public thanksgiving at Kensington Oval followed by a private service at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens.

stories.title: Honda's fixed F1 engine completes its first laps at an Aston Martin filming day — and appears to add ~30hp
stories.what_happened: Honda's newly upgraded F1 engine ran for the first time in the **AMR26** chassis during an Aston Martin filming day at the **Hungaroring**, just before F1's summer shutdown. Early reports describe the run as encouraging: the previously troublesome vibrations that had affected the car since the start of the season appear to be gone, and the update is estimated to add roughly **30 horsepower**. The upgraded engine's first competitive outing will come at the **Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort, August 21–23**, once the season resumes.

stories.title: Aston Martin's F1 paddock mourns tyre technician Mick 'Biscuit' Fern, a 35-year veteran
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin announced on Wednesday that Mick Fern, affectionately nicknamed 'Biscuit' and known across the paddock over his 35-year F1 career, had passed away. The team's statement said 'the thoughts of the entire team and F1 community are with the family and friends of our teammate.' Fern had most recently worked as one of Aston Martin's tyre technicians. His absence was visibly marked at the Hungarian Grand Prix, with the team placing a sign reading 'Biscuit. Thinking of you' outside its garage and on the grid, and figures from across the paddock gathering for a show of support. Driver Lance Stroll, who worked with Fern for seven years, said: 'You always made me laugh in the back of the garage, and you truly were one of a kind. Rest easy, Mick.'
key_points: Aston Martin tyre technician **Mick Fern**, known throughout the paddock as **'Biscuit'**, has died.
He spent **35 years in the F1 paddock**, joining the team in **1999** when it raced as Jordan.
The team announced his passing on Instagram, saying he died **'peacefully'**.
Driver **Lance Stroll** led tributes, calling him **'one of a kind'** after 7 years working together.
Teams across the grid marked his absence at the Hungarian Grand Prix with signs and shows of support.

depth.background: Behind every F1 driver is a large team of mechanics and technicians who rarely get public recognition but are essential to a car actually running — tyre technicians like Fern manage the preparation and fitting of tyres, one of the most safety-critical jobs in the pit lane. Fern's F1 career stretched back to 1999 with the Jordan team, a now-defunct outfit whose successor entities eventually became today's Aston Martin — meaning he'd been part of the same team's lineage for over a quarter-century of F1's modern era.

stories.title: Ruturaj Gaikwad named West Zone captain for the Duleep Trophy, with Prithvi Shaw earning a recall
stories.what_happened: West Zone's selectors named their squad for the **2026-27 Duleep Trophy**, appointing **Ruturaj Gaikwad** — Chennai Super Kings' IPL captain — as West Zone captain, with Mumbai all-rounder **Shams Mulani** as vice-captain. The 15-man squad also includes Shardul Thakur, Sarfaraz Khan, Musheer Khan, Tushar Deshpande and wicketkeeper Harvik Desai, with six of the fifteen players coming from Mumbai. The headline inclusion is **Prithvi Shaw**, who was left out of Mumbai's squad and instead rebuilt his case with Maharashtra, scoring **537 runs** at an average of **48.81** in his debut season for the new state — form strong enough to earn this zonal recall. The tournament begins **August 23** at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
key_points: **Ruturaj Gaikwad** will captain West Zone in the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy, with **Shams Mulani** as his deputy.
**Prithvi Shaw** earns a recall to zonal cricket after a strong debut Ranji Trophy season for Maharashtra — **537 runs** in 11 innings at an average of **48.81**.
The 15-man squad includes six Mumbai players, among them all-rounder **Shardul Thakur** and batter **Sarfaraz Khan**.
The tournament, India's season-opening first-class competition, begins **August 23** at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

National selectors have long used it as an early-season form guide before the marquee Ranji Trophy season, which is why the tournament carries extra weight for players trying to force their way back into national reckoning — like Prithvi Shaw, a former India opener who was dropped by his home state, Mumbai, and had to rebuild his case for a new state before zonal selectors took notice.

stories.title: F1 delays final call on its 2026 season finale until September, ruling out a US replacement race
stories.what_happened: Speaking this week, F1 president **Stefano Domenicali** said the sport will make its final decision on the fate of the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix in **mid-September at the earliest** — giving organizers as much time as possible to see whether the security situation in the Middle East stabilizes. He confirmed F1 remains **committed to holding both races as planned** for now, but said that if the conflict makes it impossible, the season will instead end with a race in **Europe** rather than a hastily arranged one in the United States, specifically because a new US race would clash with the **NFL season** and be difficult to schedule around. This follows the earlier cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, which were replaced by a rebranded race at **Sepang, Malaysia** in October.
key_points: F1 president **Stefano Domenicali** says a decision on the season's last two rounds won't come until **mid-September at the earliest**
Any replacement race will be held in **Europe**, not the US — F1 doesn't want to clash with the **NFL season**

F1 says it remains **committed** to holding both races in 2026 for now

depth.background: Formula 1's 2026 calendar has already been disrupted once this year: the **Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix**, originally set for April, were both cancelled after the US and Israel's strikes on Iran and the retaliation that followed made the region too dangerous to race in safely. F1 improvised by having **Sepang in Malaysia** host a race under the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' name in October instead. Now the same conflict is threatening the **final two rounds of the season**, in **Qatar and Abu Dhabi**, which are usually the championship-deciding races in November/December.

stories.title: Supreme Court strikes down the rule letting projects get environmental clearance *after* they've already started
stories.what_happened: On **July 29**, a three-judge Supreme Court bench of **Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice Vipul Pancholi** unanimously **struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum** that had let the Centre grant environmental clearance to projects **after** they had already started construction or operations. The Court held that **prior environmental clearance is the cornerstone** of India's environmental regulatory framework and cannot be sidestepped through an executive order. It ruled the government **does** have the power to permit post-facto clearances, but only if it does so through a **valid statutory notification under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — not an internal memo. Clearances already granted under the 2017 notification or the now-scrapped 2021 memo will **continue to hold**, unless separately challenged in court, and the judgment applies **prospectively** — meaning no fresh clearances can be issued through the scrapped route from here on.
key_points: The Supreme Court **quashed a 2021 Office Memorandum** that let projects get **retrospective ('post-facto') environmental clearance**.
A **three-judge bench** led by **Chief Justice Surya Kant** ruled the Centre can't create such a bypass through a mere administrative order.
The Centre **can still allow post-facto clearances**, but only through a **valid statutory notification**, not an office memo.
Clearances already granted under the **2017 notification** and the now-**quashed 2021 memo** stay valid unless individually challenged.
The ruling applies **going forward only** — no new post-facto clearances can be issued under the scrapped mechanism.

depth.background: In India, most large projects — mines, factories, power plants, real estate — legally need an **environmental clearance (EC)** *before* construction begins, to assess and limit ecological damage upfront. Some companies have started projects without this approval and then sought clearance afterward, effectively asking regulators to forgive a fait accompli. In **2021**, the central government issued an **Office Memorandum (OM)** — a lower-level administrative order, not a law — creating a formal process for exactly that kind of after-the-fact approval, which environmental groups and courts have long argued undermines the entire point of the clearance system.

stories.title: Kimi Antonelli's Hungarian GP grid penalty reignites F1's fuzzy yellow-flag rules debate
stories.what_happened: During Hungarian Grand Prix qualifying, Max Verstappen spun late in Q3, triggering a single yellow flag in that sector. FIA stewards found Kimi Antonelli did not sufficiently slow down through the flagged zone — telemetry showed he was **14 km/h slower** entering the mini-sector but **3 km/h faster** than usual by the time he passed the incident, with an overall speed reduction the FIA judged as **'less than 1%.'** He was handed a **three-place grid penalty** and one penalty point (taking him to four for the rolling 12-month period), avoiding a harsher five-place drop because stewards accepted he made some effort to slow and had limited time to react. The decision has reignited debate, with Mercedes' race engineers and George Russell pointing out that Antonelli's case looked remarkably similar to one where Russell himself avoided penalty at an earlier race in Austria.
key_points: Antonelli was hit with a **three-place grid penalty** for not slowing enough under yellow flags in Hungary qualifying.
The incident happened after **Max Verstappen spun** late in Q3, triggering a single yellow flag.
FIA telemetry showed Antonelli was **14 km/h slower** entering the flagged zone but **3 km/h faster** exiting it.
Mercedes' **George Russell** says drivers remain deeply divided on how much slowing is actually required.
The penalty adds a point to Antonelli's licence, taking him to **four** in the current 12-month window.

depth.background: Under F1's single yellow-flag rule, drivers must slow down enough to make passage through that section of track safe — but the rules don't specify exactly how much speed reduction counts as 'enough,' leaving it to race stewards to judge case by case using telemetry data. This ambiguity has caused recurring controversy over the years, with drivers arguing the standard is applied inconsistently between similar incidents. Kimi Antonelli is Mercedes' young driver currently leading the 2026 drivers' championship, making any penalty to him especially consequential to the title fight.

stories.title: Ryan ten Doeschate quits as India's assistant coach — and resurfaces at Knight Riders a day later

stories.title: F1 sets mid-September deadline to decide fate of Qatar and Abu Dhabi season finales
stories.what_happened: F1 boss Stefano Domenicali confirmed the sport will wait until mid-September at the earliest to decide whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix, both scheduled to close out the 2026 season, can be safely held given the security situation in the Middle East. stories.title: Sachin Siwach storms into Commonwealth Games boxing quarter-finals as Lovlina Borgohain gets a bye into hers

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton locks in a third season at Ferrari by hitting his contract's performance target
stories.what_happened: Hamilton has now **activated that clause**, securing a guaranteed **third season with Ferrari**, after meeting the contract's performance conditions — helped by his current **P2 championship standing**. stories.title: Red Bull wants to lock down Max Verstappen through 2029 — right as his contract's exit door swings open
stories.what_happened: Red Bull has opened talks to extend Verstappen's contract by an additional season, from its current 2028 expiry to **2029**, which would give him **14 consecutive seasons** with the team. But the timing is notable: Verstappen's existing deal contains an **exit clause** that activates if he isn't inside the **top two** of the drivers' championship by the summer break — and he is currently **sixth**, meaning he could walk away from Red Bull entirely rather than sign anything new. Reports describe the ball as being in **Verstappen's camp**, with no indication yet of which way he's leaning.
key_points: **Red Bull** is trying to extend **Max Verstappen's** contract, which runs to **2028**, by one more year to **2029**.

Verstappen's current deal has an **exit clause** letting him leave if he's outside the **top two** in the standings at the summer break.

stories.title: Congress moves to force a Lok Sabha debate on the Ram Mandir donation-fraud scandal, demands a Supreme Court-judge probe
stories.what_happened: On July 29, Congress MP **KC Venugopal** gave notice of an adjournment motion in the Lok Sabha — a procedural move to halt regular business and force an immediate debate — over what he called "massive financial fraud and embezzlement" of public donations at the Ram Mandir. This follows an earlier letter Venugopal sent Prime Minister Modi around July 20 making the same demand. Congress argues the SIT's arrests so far — **8 low-level staff**, with about **₹80 lakh** recovered from six of them — are "eyewash" that protects more powerful people, pointing to the deletion of **7 to 8 months of CCTV footage** and the earlier removal of a Chief Accounts Officer who had flagged irregularities as far back as **2020–21**. Trust general secretary Champat Rai, who resigned July 6 and was replaced by Bajrang Bangara, has broken his silence to deny personal wrongdoing, saying he will address the allegations in full once the SIT submits its final report.

depth.background: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust runs the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, the temple built on a site at the center of decades of religious and political conflict in India and a flagship project closely associated with the ruling BJP and Prime Minister Modi. Since the temple opened, it has drawn enormous cash and jewellery donations from pilgrims. In June, reports surfaced alleging a **coordinated racket siphoning off donations**, prompting Uttar Pradesh's state government to form a **Special Investigation Team (SIT)** on June 13 and register an FIR on June 25. The Trust accepted Champat Rai's resignation on July 6 and began restructuring its administration, including plans to hire a professional CEO.

stories.title: India's Foreign Secretary wraps up a two-day Beijing visit aimed at steadying ties with China
stories.what_happened: Misri began his engagements on **July 28** with a meeting with **Sun Haiyan**, Vice Minister of the International Department of China's Communist Party, where the two discussed implementing guidance from both countries' leaderships to improve relations — including more political engagement, people-to-people contacts, and academic/think-tank exchanges. He then met **Hua Chunying**, China's Vice Foreign Minister, reviewing the full range of bilateral issues and exploring ways to advance the idea that India and China should see each other as **partners rather than rivals**, with a focus on mutually beneficial trade and economic cooperation. The visit concluded on **July 29**.

He met **Sun Haiyan**, Vice Minister of the Chinese Communist Party's International Department, on July 28.

depth.background: India and China, the world's two most populous nations, fought a deadly border clash in the Galwan Valley in 2020 that froze high-level diplomatic and economic ties for years. Relations have been thawing gradually since then, with both sides restoring some direct flights, easing visa rules, and resuming senior-level talks — while the underlying border dispute in the Himalayas remains unresolved. **Vikram Misri**, India's top career diplomat as Foreign Secretary, has been a key figure managing this delicate reset.

stories.title: Asian Paints' profit jumps 40% as India Inc.'s biggest earnings day gets underway

stories.title: Sensex jumps over 800 points, Nifty back above 24,200 as IT stocks rally and crude rebounds

The past week has seen sharp crude volatility tied to the escalating US-Iran standoff in the Middle East, whipsawing sentiment across Indian markets.

stories.title: Lok Sabha passes tougher anti-paper-leak bill amid uproar over Rahul Gandhi's 'shooting' claim
stories.what_happened: The Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 by voice vote on Wednesday, despite repeated disruptions. The bill sets stricter penalties — up to **10 years in prison** and fines as high as **₹10 crore**, plus asset confiscation — for those convicted of leaking exam papers or otherwise cheating public examinations. It also imposes firm timelines: leak investigations must be completed within two months, and trials must conclude within three. The debate itself was overshadowed by a separate political clash, after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused Home Minister Amit Shah of ordering police to fire on students during a July 20 protest march, which the government denied.
key_points: Lok Sabha passed the **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026** by voice vote
Punishment rises to up to **10 years in jail** and fines up to **₹10 crore**, with confiscation of assets
New deadlines require paper-leak **investigations to finish in 2 months** and trials in **3 months**
The bill follows nationwide protests over the **NEET-UG 2026** exam leak, which forced education minister **Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation**
Passage came amid a Lok Sabha uproar after **Rahul Gandhi** accused the government of ordering pellet-gun fire on protesting students

depth.background: The bill amends the existing Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, which was already meant to deter exam-paper leaks but has failed to stop repeated scandals. The latest and biggest trigger was the **NEET-UG 2026** medical entrance exam leak, which set off nationwide student protests and ultimately cost education minister Dharmendra Pradhan his job. Union Minister Jitendra Singh introduced the amendment bill days after the protests, and it was taken up for debate this week during Parliament's monsoon session.
