stories.title: Audi's Bortoleto says his 2027 future is 'already sorted' as Sainz's Williams seat stays in doubt
stories.what_happened: Bortoleto confirmed publicly that his position at Audi is locked in beyond 2027, closing off one seat some had speculated Sainz might target. That leaves Sainz weighing his limited options: staying at a struggling Williams, or a long-shot Audi move complicated by Hulkenberg's existing contract through 2027. Separately, reports note Fernando Alonso is likely to stay at Aston Martin through 2027 if the team's competitive form improves, while Franco Colapinto's seat is described as at risk in some team-reshuffle scenarios, with a return to Williams floated as one landing spot.
key_points: Audi driver **Gabriel Bortoleto** says he's signed with the team **'for many years'** and his 2027 seat is settled.
That narrows the field just as **Carlos Sainz** weighs his own future amid **Williams' poor form** since the 2026 rules reset.
Sainz is still linked to **Audi**, but teammate-designate **Nico Hulkenberg** is contracted there through **2027**.
**Fernando Alonso** is likely to stay at Aston Martin through 2027 if the team's form holds up.
**Franco Colapinto** could lose his current seat in some scenarios, with a Williams return floated as a fallback.

depth.background: F1's 2027 driver market is unusually fluid because several teams — Audi (the rebranded Sauber works team), Williams, and Aston Martin — are all still settling their long-term line-ups following the sport's 2026 rules reset, which reshuffled the competitive order. Carlos Sainz joined Williams for 2025 expecting the team to be competitive under new rules, but Williams has struggled, fueling speculation he could look elsewhere for 2027.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi accuses Amit Shah of ordering students to be shot; government denies it
stories.what_happened: During Wednesday's Lok Sabha debate on the anti-paper-leak bill, Rahul Gandhi said Home Minister Amit Shah had 'ordered the shooting of our students' and put 'pellets into the blood of our students' during the July 20 march, triggering a major uproar in the House. Union Minister Jitendra Singh directly rejected the claim, stating no shots were fired and that only tear gas was used to disperse the crowd. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju called the allegation a serious breach of Gandhi's own position and privilege, and demanded he apologise. The exchange repeatedly disrupted proceedings even as the underlying bill was ultimately passed.
key_points: Rahul Gandhi told the Lok Sabha that Home Minister **Amit Shah 'ordered the shooting'** of protesting students
He said police put **'pellets into the blood'** of students during the **July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march** at Jantar Mantar
Minister **Jitendra Singh** rejected the claim, saying **no shots were fired** and only tear gas was used
Parliamentary Affairs Minister **Kiren Rijiju** demanded Gandhi **apologise**, calling it a breach of privilege
The clash erupted during debate on the **anti-paper-leak bill**, tied to the same NEET-UG protest movement

depth.background: The allegation stems from the wave of student protests that followed the NEET-UG 2026 exam-leak scandal. On July 20, students marched on Parliament in a 'Sansad Chalo' demonstration demanding accountability; the government says police used tear gas to control the crowd, while opposition figures have alleged more forceful tactics were used, including pellet guns. Rahul Gandhi, as Leader of the Opposition, has positioned himself as a vocal defender of the protesting students throughout this episode.

stories.title: India's economy sends mixed signals as a weak monsoon and trade shocks offset falling oil prices
stories.what_happened: A Bloomberg review of India's economy published **July 29** found the picture is genuinely mixed: government capital spending has slowed and fewer new infrastructure projects are being announced, both of which usually signal softer near-term growth. At the same time, **June rainfall came in around 40% below normal**, and some forecasters now warn the eventual monsoon shortfall could be worse than the **10% deficit** currently built into official projections — a serious risk given how much of Indian agriculture depends on the rains. Set against that, falling **global oil prices** are helping India, a major crude importer, by lowering its import bill and easing some inflation pressure. The RBI has publicly maintained that the domestic economy remains resilient despite the Iran-war and tariff-related uncertainty.
key_points: **Slow government spending** and fewer new project announcements are weighing on India's growth outlook.
**June rainfall ran ~40% below normal**, with forecasters warning the monsoon shortfall could beat the **10% deficit** currently projected.
A weak monsoon threatens to **curb crop output, push up food prices, and squeeze rural incomes** — a large share of India's population depends on farm income.
The **RBI** (India's central bank) says the economy has stayed **resilient** through the Iran war and tariff shocks so far.
Falling global **oil prices** are a rare tailwind, cutting India's import bill since it buys most of its crude abroad.

depth.background: India's growth engine runs on a delicate balance: strong domestic demand and services growth on one side, and the **monsoon** (June–September rains that irrigate most Indian farmland) and global trade conditions on the other. This year, India is also absorbing the shock of new US tariffs and elevated oil-price volatility tied to the **Iran war**, both of which the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has flagged as key risks to watch. A poor monsoon hits India differently than most economies because so much of rural income and food-price inflation depends directly on rainfall.

stories.title: Deep depression crosses into Odisha-Bengal near Digha, flash-flood red alert issued for 27 Odisha districts
stories.what_happened: The deep depression crossed the West Bengal coast near Digha shortly after midnight and has since moved west-northwestward over northern interior Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal. The India Meteorological Department issued a **red warning** for Sundargarh, Kendujhar and Mayurbhanj districts for Wednesday, while Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner directed collectors in **27 of the state's 30 districts** to stay on high alert for flash-flood-like conditions. Isolated pockets could see rainfall in excess of **204.5mm**. Schools were shut in several affected districts as a precaution, and fishermen have been told to stay off the northwest Bay of Bengal and the Odisha-Bengal-north Andhra coast through the morning of July 29.
key_points: The system made landfall near **Digha** on the West Bengal coast just after midnight
IMD issued a **red alert** — its highest warning — for Sundargarh, Kendujhar and Mayurbhanj
**27 of Odisha's 30 districts** have been placed on flash-flood alert by the state government
Rainfall could exceed **204.5mm** in isolated pockets through July 29–30
Schools shut in Mayurbhanj, Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts as a precaution

depth.background: This weather system formed over the northwest Bay of Bengal and intensified into a deep depression before crossing the coast — the same system we covered making landfall near Haldia on July 28. Since then it has continued pushing inland across Odisha and Gangetic West Bengal at roughly **12km/h**, dragging its heavy-rain band with it. This comes on the heels of Assam's floods earlier this month, which killed dozens and displaced hundreds of thousands, making this eastern-India monsoon stretch an unusually punishing one.

thread.previously: We reported the system crossed the coast near Haldia on the morning of July 28, with a red alert for three districts and ten Odisha districts flagged for heavy rain.
thread.changed: The system has since pushed further inland, and the flash-flood alert has widened dramatically to 27 of Odisha's 30 districts, with several districts closing schools as a precaution.

stories.title: F1's 2027 driver market domino chain: Alonso's next move could decide seats at Williams, Alpine and Haas
stories.what_happened: Paddock reporting suggests Alonso's decision on where he races in 2027 is now the key that unlocks several other seats. **Franco Colapinto**, currently at Alpine, was seen having dinner with Williams team principal **James Vowles**, fuelling speculation he could return to Williams — the team he raced for in 2025 — if Alonso takes over his Alpine seat. Separately, **Esteban Ocon's** position at Haas looks vulnerable: he has scored only **3 points** this season compared to teammate **Ollie Bearman's 13**. Both **Carlos Sainz** and Ocon are being mentioned as candidates to replace Alonso at **Aston Martin** if he leaves. Meanwhile **Sergio Perez** is reportedly being evaluated by three different teams — Williams, Aston Martin, and Alpine — as a fallback signing.
key_points: **Fernando Alonso's** choice of team for 2027 is expected to trigger a **domino effect** across several grids
**Franco Colapinto** was seen dining with Williams boss **James Vowles** — a hint he could return there if Alonso takes his Alpine seat
**Esteban Ocon's** Haas seat looks shaky after just **3 points** this season versus teammate **Ollie Bearman's 13**
**Carlos Sainz** and **Esteban Ocon** are both floated as possible replacements for Alonso at **Aston Martin**
**Sergio Perez** is being eyed as a fallback option by **three teams** — Williams, Aston Martin and Alpine

depth.background: Formula 1's driver market runs on a web of interlocking contracts — when one high-profile driver moves, it frequently forces a chain reaction as teams scramble to fill the resulting vacancy, and the drivers who lose out chase the next-best seat elsewhere. Going into the 2026 season's back half, a wave of contracts are expiring for 2027, and **Fernando Alonso**, a two-time world champion now racing for Alpine, is one of the biggest names still undecided about his future — making him the trigger point for several other teams' plans.

stories.title: Shubman Gill becomes India's fourth-ever No.1 ranked ODI batter as Siraj tops the bowling charts too
stories.what_happened: Following his performances in India's recent ODI series in England — including an unbeaten 80 in the first match and 77 at Lord's in the third — **Shubman Gill** overtook Babar Azam to claim the **No.1 spot in the ICC ODI batting rankings**, becoming just the fourth Indian to do so after Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni and Virat Kohli. In the same rankings update, **Mohammed Siraj** rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**, giving India the top spot in both disciplines at once. Separately, 15-year-old **Vaibhav Suryavanshi** jumped 230 places in the T20I batting rankings, reflecting his rapid rise through IPL and youth-cricket performances.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** dethroned Babar Azam to become the world's **No.1 ranked ODI batter**.
**Mohammed Siraj** simultaneously rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**.
Gill is only the **fourth Indian ever** to hold the top ODI batting spot, after Tendulkar, Dhoni and Kohli.
The rise came on the back of Gill's England ODI series form, including scores of **80 not out and 77**.
Teenager **Vaibhav Suryavanshi jumped 230 places** in the T20I batting rankings on the same list update.

depth.background: The **ICC Player Rankings** are updated regularly using a points system that weighs recent performances, opposition strength and match context, and reaching No.1 in any format is considered one of the clearest statistical markers of a player's current form. Gill has been closing in on the top ODI spot for weeks; Babar Azam had held it before him.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian city again, damage a 7th Wildberries warehouse; woman killed in Taganrog
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian drones struck **industrial facilities in Ryazan**, a city roughly 200 km southeast of Moscow, on **July 29**. The regional governor said the strikes started fires and that **six people** required medical attention. Among the sites hit was a **Wildberries warehouse** — the **seventh** of the e-commerce giant's facilities damaged in a wave of recent attacks. In a separate incident the same day, a **woman was killed** and a man injured in the southern port city of **Taganrog** on the Sea of Azov, after **missile debris** struck an apartment building. Russian authorities confirmed both incidents.
key_points: Ukrainian drones struck **industrial sites in Ryazan**, a Russian city southeast of Moscow, sparking fires
A **Wildberries warehouse** was damaged — the **7th** of the Russian retailer's facilities hit in recent days
**Six people** in Ryazan sought medical attention after the strikes, the regional governor said
Separately, a **woman was killed** and a man injured when **missile debris** struck an apartment building in **Taganrog**
Part of Ukraine's escalating **'deep strike' campaign** targeting Russian industrial, logistics, and energy sites

depth.background: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in **February 2022**, both sides have increasingly used long-range drones and missiles to strike targets far from the front line — Russia hitting Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, and Ukraine hitting Russian oil refineries, military plants, and now warehouses and logistics hubs. Through 2026 Ukraine has scaled up these '**deep strike**' attacks, aiming to disrupt the Russian economy and supply chains that support the war effort rather than just battlefield targets. Wildberries, one of Russia's largest online retailers, has seen a string of its warehouses damaged in these strikes in recent days, making it a recurring target.

stories.title: Hamilton says Ferrari must close a straight-line speed gap to fight for the F1 title in the second half
stories.what_happened: Heading into Formula 1's summer break, **Hamilton** is second in the drivers' championship, **50 points** behind leader **Kimi Antonelli**, and **31 points** behind Ferrari teammate **Charles Leclerc**, who won the **British Grand Prix** this year while Hamilton took his own win at the **Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix** in June. Hamilton said Ferrari's main weakness has been straight-line speed, estimating the car has been **three to four tenths of a second down** on power and pace compared to rivals for the season's first half. He pointed to Ferrari winning **two of the last three races** as evidence the team is closing that gap, and said he feels **more focused than ever** going into the second half of the season.
key_points: Hamilton sits **second** in the drivers' championship, **50 points** behind runaway leader Antonelli
He's just **31 points** behind teammate **Charles Leclerc**, who won the **British Grand Prix**
Hamilton says Ferrari has been **three to four tenths down** on the straights in pace and power all season
Ferrari has won **two of the last three races**, a sign the car is closing the competitive gap
Hamilton says he's '**more focused than ever**' heading into the season's second half

depth.background: Formula 1's season splits into two halves around a summer break, giving teams a rare pause to regroup and plan upgrades before the run to the championship. **Lewis Hamilton**, a seven-time world champion, joined Ferrari for the 2025 season hoping to end the team's long title drought; his 2026 campaign has been solid but not dominant, sitting behind both championship leader Kimi Antonelli and his own teammate Charles Leclerc for parts of the year.

stories.title: Ryan ten Doeschate returns to Knight Riders as head of cricket strategy across all franchises
stories.what_happened: Knight Riders Sports announced Ryan ten Doeschate as its new Head of Cricket Strategy, a role that will oversee scouting, player recruitment, squad planning and performance evaluation across its four global franchises: Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL, Trinbago Knight Riders in the CPL, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the ILT20, and Los Angeles Knight Riders in the MLC. Alongside the strategy role, he will also work as assistant coach for the CPL, ILT20 and MLC teams specifically. The appointment follows his exit as assistant coach of the India men's team, a position he held for two years. He was a title-winning player for KKR in IPL 2012 and 2014, and was part of the support staff for their third title in 2024.
key_points: **Ryan ten Doeschate** is Knight Riders Sports' new **Head of Cricket Strategy**, overseeing scouting and squad planning across all its teams
That covers **Kolkata Knight Riders (IPL)**, **Trinbago Knight Riders (CPL)**, **Abu Dhabi Knight Riders (ILT20)** and **Los Angeles Knight Riders (MLC)**

The move comes right after he **stepped down as India men's team assistant coach**, a role he held for two years
Ten Doeschate previously won **two IPL titles as a KKR player (2012, 2014)** and a third as **support staff in 2024**

Ten Doeschate's ties to the group go back to 2011 as a KKR player, and he later moved into coaching there in 2022 before joining India's men's team as assistant coach for two years, a post he has now left.

stories.title: Assam flood toll climbs to 75 as seven more die in Sivasagar, 3.32 lakh people affected
stories.what_happened: Assam's government confirmed the flood death toll has reached **75** after **seven** more people drowned in **Sivasagar district**. More than **3.32 lakh (332,000) people** remain affected across seven districts — Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sonitpur and Kamrup Metropolitan. In response, Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** announced an increase in compensation for families of the deceased to **₹9 lakh**, and said more than **one lakh** of the worst-affected households have already received **₹15,000** each in immediate cash relief.
key_points: Assam's flood death toll has risen to **75** after **seven** fresh drowning deaths in Sivasagar district
More than **3.32 lakh people** remain affected across **seven districts**
Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** raised compensation for bereaved families to **₹9 lakh**
Over **one lakh** severely-hit households have received **₹15,000** each for immediate relief
Sivasagar, Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sonitpur and Kamrup Metropolitan remain the worst-hit districts

depth.background: Assam floods almost every monsoon season (roughly **June to September**) as the Brahmaputra river and its tributaries swell with heavy rain and water flowing down from upstream in the eastern Himalayas. The state's low-lying floodplains, dense population, and river-erosion patterns mean floods regularly displace hundreds of thousands of people and damage crops, roads and homes. This year's flooding has been building for weeks, with the death toll climbing steadily as more casualties are confirmed from remote, hard-to-reach areas.

stories.title: Bumrah's Sri Lanka Test fate now hinges on an August 7 practice match in Colombo
stories.what_happened: New reporting details the specific mechanism that will decide whether **Bumrah** plays in India's upcoming Sri Lanka Test series: a **practice match in Colombo beginning August 7** is now understood to be the actual test of his readiness, rather than a simple fitness scan. That leaves only **eight days** between that practice match and the first Test, which starts **August 15 in Galle** (the second Test follows August 23 in Colombo). Bumrah has been resting his knee since injuring it fielding in the second ODI against England at Cardiff, with medical staff advising a full rest period until **July 30** before he reports to the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru for rehab and reassessment. All-rounder **Ravindra Jadeja**, who had also been on a fitness watch after an IPL 2026 elbow injury, has already been cleared and is back in the squad.
key_points: A **practice match in Colombo starting August 7** will be the real decider on Bumrah's fitness
That's just **eight days** before the first Test begins in **Galle on August 15**
Bumrah hurt his knee fielding in the **second ODI vs England** in Cardiff; swelling ruled him out of the third

**Ravindra Jadeja** has already been declared fit and is back in the squad after IPL 2026 elbow trouble

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler, and his fitness has been carefully managed for years due to a history of back and workload issues. He picked up a knee injury while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff, and it worsened enough to rule him out of the following match. India's squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka — captained by Shubman Gill, with KL Rahul as deputy — was already named on July 26, with Bumrah included but explicitly marked as fitness-dependent, and Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna named as pace backups in case he isn't ready.

thread.changed: It has now emerged that a practice match in Colombo starting August 7 — just eight days before the series opener — will be the real test of his fitness, leaving a very tight window to build match fitness before Galle.

stories.title: India Inc.'s biggest earnings day of the season: Asian Paints, Dabur and 100+ companies report today
stories.what_happened: Wednesday, July 29 is one of the year's busiest results days, with **Asian Paints, Dabur India, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Eicher Motors and Waaree Energies** among the companies due to report Q1 FY27 numbers. Brokerages expect **Asian Paints** to show 14–17% year-on-year revenue growth on the back of 2–4% price hikes taken in June and dealers stocking up ahead of them, though margins may come in flat to slightly lower as crude-linked raw material costs rose during the quarter. **Dabur** has already signaled roughly double-digit revenue and profit growth in a pre-results update, with India volumes up about 5% and rural demand outpacing urban demand for a second consecutive quarter. **Thursday (July 30) is even bigger** — Bajaj Finance, Tata Steel, Maruti Suzuki and Sun Pharma are all due

stories.title: Iran says US strikes wrecked Bushehr airport, killed over 350 government workers
stories.what_happened: Iran's government published a detailed account of infrastructure destroyed by US strikes over the past two weeks. It says **Bushehr airport is completely inoperable** and a newly purchased aircraft was destroyed there, along with damage to the Bandar Abbas railway and airports at Iranshahr, Semnan and Bandar Abbas. The government also claims **more than 350 of its employees were killed**, though this figure has not been independently confirmed by outside observers. Separately, Russia has pulled another 163 staff out of the nearby Bushehr nuclear plant as a precaution, leaving about 300 personnel there. The US has not officially confirmed casualty figures or commented on this specific report.
key_points: Iranian officials say US strikes destroyed **Bushehr airport**, which they say must be rebuilt from scratch
The government says **over 350 government employees** were killed in the campaign — a toll Reuters says it could not independently verify
**12 bridges**, two tunnels, a marine control tower and a weather station were also damaged, per Tehran
Russia has evacuated **163 more staff** from Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, leaving roughly 300 personnel still on site
This is Iran's **first detailed public accounting** of war damage since the informal pause took hold

depth.background: The US and Iran have been in an undeclared conflict since February 2026, triggered by Iranian-linked attacks on shipping in the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes. The US and allies responded with strikes on Iranian military sites and infrastructure. Fighting has recently eased into an informal pause, but Tehran has refused to sign onto any formal ceasefire, leaving the truce fragile. Russia, which helped build and staff Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant, has a direct stake in how the damage assessment plays out.

stories.title: A brush-on liquid stopped tooth decay in more than half of treated baby teeth in a major US trial — no drilling required
stories.what_happened: Researchers led by the **University of Michigan** ran a randomized Phase III clinical trial enrolling **830 children younger than 6**, recruited through dental offices, pediatric medical practices, and Head Start / Early Head Start programs across Michigan, New York, and Iowa. Children in the trial had a **38% SDF solution** brushed directly onto their decayed baby teeth every six months. The study, published in **JAMA Pediatrics**, found the treatment arrested decay in **more than half** of the treated teeth — stopping the cavity from getting worse without any drilling, injections, or sedation. The one tradeoff: SDF permanently **stains the treated area black**, since it works partly by reacting with the tooth's minerals. Researchers say this is the kind of large US population trial the FDA needs to formally evaluate SDF as an approved drug for treating cavities, rather than an off-label technique.
key_points: A **Phase III trial of 830 children** under 6 found that silver diamine fluoride (SDF) arrested decay in **more than half** of treated baby teeth
The treatment is a liquid **brushed onto the cavity in seconds** — no drilling, needles, or sedation needed
It was tested at **6-month intervals** using a **38% SDF** solution
Led by the **University of Michigan**, recruiting through dental and pediatric offices and Head Start programs in Michigan, New York, and Iowa
The trial gives the FDA the large-scale US safety and efficacy data it needs to formally approve SDF as a **drug** for treating cavities

depth.background: Cavities in baby teeth are extremely common, and the standard fix — drilling out the decay and filling it — is often traumatic for young children, sometimes requiring sedation or general anesthesia. **Silver diamine fluoride (SDF)** is a liquid that has been used for decades in other countries, including Japan, as a simple way to stop decay from spreading without removing any tooth material. It has lacked the large, rigorous **US clinical trials** regulators need before approving it as an official treatment, which is why many American dentists have only offered it informally or as a stopgap.

stories.title: US and Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed sites in Iraq after a fresh wave of drone attacks
stories.what_happened: CENTCOM said US and Saudi aircraft struck multiple **logistics and weapons sites in eastern Iraq** on Tuesday evening, July 28, in response to more than **30 drone attacks directed by the IRGC** against US-linked positions over the prior three days. The response came hours after Iran's own ballistic missile attack on US forces was intercepted, and roughly a day after President Trump said Washington had halted its bombing campaign because Iran 'wanted to talk' — a claim Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei publicly disputed, saying **'we have no negotiations with the United States at present.'** CENTCOM added that '**the IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response.**' Iranian officials condemned the Iraq strikes as a dangerous escalation and a breach of Iraqi sovereignty. Trump, writing online, warned Iran not to counter-attack, saying the US would respond with **'a force that has never been seen.'** The exchange followed closely on Trump's White House meetings with Israeli PM Netanyahu and Ukraine's Zelensky, both described by the administration as 'positive and productive.'
key_points: US and Saudi fighter jets hit **logistics and weapons sites** in eastern Iraq used by Iran-backed militias
The strikes answered **more than 30 drone attacks** on US-linked targets over the previous 72 hours
Trump publicly warned Iran '**THEY BETTER NOT**' retaliate, threatening a response 'never before seen'
Iran called the joint strikes a '**highly dangerous escalation**' and a violation of Iraqi sovereignty
The renewed fighting came **a day after** Trump said the US had paused its bombing campaign on Iran

depth.background: Since a wave of **Iranian ballistic missiles targeted US forces in the Middle East on July 28** (intercepted, no injuries, oil jumped about 5%), the region has swung between brief pauses and fresh flare-ups. The underlying conflict began after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (**IRGC**) and allied militias in Iraq, Lebanon and Yemen escalated attacks on US and Israeli-linked targets, and Washington answered with strikes of its own. Iraq's Kurdistan region has separately absorbed a string of Iranian drone and missile strikes on Kurdish dissident camps this month, showing how the fighting keeps spilling beyond Iran's own borders. Trump has run a dual track — talking about negotiations one day, ordering strikes the next — which both sides say has made the situation genuinely unpredictable.

thread.previously: Iran's IRGC fired up to four ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East on July 28; all were intercepted with no injuries, and oil jumped about 5% on fears the recent calm was fraying.
thread.changed: The US and Saudi Arabia hit back directly, striking Iran-backed logistics and weapons sites in Iraq in response to over 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks in 72 hours, and Trump issued a public warning against any Iranian counter-strike.

stories.title: OpenAI opens its priciest AI model for free to 100,000 scientists — a $250 million bet on speeding up research
stories.what_happened: OpenAI announced on **July 29** a new program called 'ChatGPT for Academic Researchers,' offering free access to its most capable models — including **GPT-5.6 Sol Pro** — to as many as **100,000 scientists, mathematicians and engineers** worldwide. The rollout begins with **10,000 participants** this summer, scaling up through 2027. To be eligible, applicants must verify their institutional affiliation through an identity service called SheerID and have published a paper within the last three years on **arXiv, bioRxiv or ChemRxiv** in one of seven fields, including biology, chemistry, computer science, physics and engineering. Participants get expanded deep-research tools, higher usage limits and larger context windows across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI frames this as part of a **commitment worth more than $250 million** through 2027 to support scientific discovery, and says researchers' data will not be used to train its models by default.
key_points: OpenAI will give **100,000 scientists, mathematicians and engineers** free access to its top models by 2027.
The rollout starts this summer with **10,000 researchers**, including its flagship **GPT-5.6 Sol Pro** model.
It's part of a **$250 million-plus commitment** through 2027 to support outside scientific research.
To qualify, researchers need a **verified university affiliation** and a paper published in the last **3 years**.
OpenAI says researcher data **won't be used to train its models** by default.

depth.background: Frontier AI models like OpenAI's GPT-5.6 are normally metered and expensive to use at scale, which puts them out of reach for many academic labs. OpenAI has increasingly framed itself as a tool for accelerating science, not just a consumer chatbot maker. This move lands amid intensifying competition: Chinese lab Moonshot's **free Kimi K3 model** recently jumped to No. 1 on a major AI coding leaderboard, beating both OpenAI and Anthropic's best, and OpenAI separately cut prices on its cheaper models this week — signs of a broader price and access war among AI labs.

stories.title: F1 sets a September deadline to decide if its season finale moves out of the Middle East
stories.what_happened: Formula 1 has told teams it will make a final decision on the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix by **mid-September**, based on how the regional security situation develops. If the races are judged unsafe to hold, F1 has said it will shift its season finale to **Europe** rather than find another venue further afield — partly because a like-for-like replacement is hard to source on short notice, and partly to avoid clashing with the NFL season in the US, which rules out adding an extra American round. **Imola**, the Italian circuit that lost its slot on the 2026 calendar, has emerged as the leading candidate to host a replacement European finale despite it being an unusual time of year, weather-wise, for the track.
key_points: F1 has set a **mid-September deadline** to decide the fate of the season-ending **Qatar and Abu Dhabi** Grands Prix
If those races can't safely go ahead, F1 will end the 2026 season with a **European race instead**
**Imola**, dropped from this year's calendar, is the leading candidate to host a replacement finale
The uncertainty follows the earlier cancellation of the **Bahrain and Saudi Arabian** Grands Prix this season over the **US-Iran conflict**
Both Qatar and Abu Dhabi remain on the calendar and are **already sold out**

depth.background: F1's calendar has leaned increasingly on Middle East races in recent years — Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi have all hosted rounds, drawn by state investment and glamorous season-finale slots. That bet has run into trouble in 2026: escalating regional tension tied to the **US-Iran conflict** already forced F1 to scrap the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian rounds earlier this season. Qatar and Abu Dhabi, scheduled to close out the year, are now the ones in question, and F1 has been monitoring the security situation rather than committing to a call either way.

stories.title: Cadillac's F1 team allegedly tells UK staff: move to America or lose your job
stories.what_happened: Reports emerged that **Cadillac's Formula 1 team has told UK-based staff they must relocate to the United States or lose their jobs**, as the team works to consolidate operations closer to its American ownership and market. This comes as the team, in its **debut 2026 F1 season** with drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez, has struggled on track — both cars have qualified and finished races near the back of the field at recent Grands Prix, including Hungary and Belgium. The relocation push suggests Cadillac wants a more US-centered engineering and operations base for the long term, even though much of its early hiring, like most new F1 teams, likely drew on the UK's deep pool of Formula 1 engineering talent.
key_points: Cadillac's Formula 1 team is reportedly **relocating operations to the US**, its home market, as it settles into its debut season.
UK-based staff have allegedly been told they must **relocate to America or be let go**.
The team, fielding **Valtteri Bottas and Sergio 'Checo' Perez**, is competing in its first-ever F1 season in 2026.
Cadillac's on-track results have been rough so far, with both cars starting recent races **near the back of the grid**.
The relocation report adds workforce uncertainty on top of the team's on-track struggles in its debut year.

depth.background: **Cadillac**, the American luxury brand owned by General Motors, joined Formula 1 as an entirely new team for the 2026 season — the first new constructor entry in years, following through on a long approval process with F1's governing bodies. It signed two experienced drivers, 10-time race winner Valtteri Bottas and six-time race winner Sergio Perez, to lead the new outfit. New F1 teams typically build their initial engineering base wherever they can hire experienced staff fastest — often the UK, home to most of F1's specialist supply chain — even if the team's brand and ownership are American.

stories.title: Microsoft's Azure cloud business blows past forecasts, adding roughly $260 billion in market value overnight
stories.what_happened: Microsoft reported fiscal fourth-quarter results after markets closed on July 29, posting **$90.01 billion in revenue**, an 18% jump from a year earlier and about $2.4 billion ahead of analyst estimates. **Azure's growth accelerated to 43%**, clearing its own guidance range and pushing Azure's full-year revenue past **$100 billion** for the first time in the division's history. GAAP earnings per share rose 32% to $4.81, while adjusted EPS of $4.74 beat expectations by roughly 12%. The stock surged in after-hours and premarket trading — estimates ranged from **7% to 14%** — adding an estimated **$260 billion** to Microsoft's market capitalization in a single session, one of the largest one-day value gains for any company this year.
key_points: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 revenue hit **$90.01 billion**, up **18%** year-over-year and well above Wall Street's estimate.
**Azure cloud revenue growth accelerated to 43%**, its fastest pace in years, pushing full-year Azure sales past **$100 billion** for the first time.
Adjusted earnings per share came in at **$4.74**, beating estimates by about **12%**.
The stock jumped as much as **7–14%** in after-hours trading, adding roughly **$260 billion** in market value in a single evening.
The results are read as proof that Microsoft's **massive AI infrastructure spending is starting to generate real returns**.

depth.background: Microsoft, along with Amazon and Google, has spent well over $100 billion combined in recent years building data centers and buying AI chips to power cloud services and AI tools like Copilot. Investors have been anxiously watching quarterly earnings from these companies for proof that this spending is actually paying off in higher revenue, rather than just being a costly bet on AI's future. Azure is Microsoft's cloud-computing division and its biggest growth engine, competing directly with Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud.

stories.title: Shubman Gill reclaims the No. 1 spot in ICC's ODI batting rankings
stories.what_happened: Shubman Gill reclaimed the No. 1 ranking among ODI batters after a strong showing in India's recently concluded series against England, where he scored 188 runs across three matches. He leapfrogged New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell, who had held the top spot since January but slipped after being ruled out of the final ODI against West Indies in Bridgetown with a low-grade hip strain. This marks Gill's third stint at the top of the ODI rankings, and comes with his career tally now at 3,379 runs in 67 ODIs, including 9 centuries and 20 half-centuries.
key_points: Gill returned to **No. 1** in the ICC ODI batting rankings, his **third spell** at the top.
He overtook New Zealand's **Daryl Mitchell**, who dropped from the top spot after being ruled out of a Bridgetown ODI with a hip strain.
Gill's rise follows a strong run against England, where he scored **188 runs in 3 matches**.
He now has **3,379 runs in 67 ODIs**, including **9 centuries** and **20 half-centuries**.
Gill captains both India's ODI and Test sides, adding weight to his status as the team's batting anchor across formats.

depth.background: The ICC batting rankings are a running points system based on recent performances, weighted more heavily toward matches against strong opposition and in bigger tournaments. Shubman Gill has held the ODI No. 1 spot before, but lost it earlier this year as other batters, including New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell, went on stronger streaks. Gill was named India's ODI and Test captain in 2026, putting extra scrutiny on his own batting form as he leads both sides.

stories.title: A drone hits a US-owned gas tanker at Egypt's Damietta port, widening the Iran war to a new country
stories.what_happened: On **Wednesday, July 29**, a drone struck the **Energos Winter**, a floating storage and regasification unit (a **ship that stores and converts liquefied natural gas back into usable gas**) docked at Egypt's Damietta port on the Mediterranean coast. The fire spread to a nearby vessel, the **Gaslog Salem**. Egyptian authorities confirmed a preliminary investigation found the blaze was caused by a drone, and said port operations continued despite the attack with no casualties reported. No group has claimed responsibility — Yemen's Houthi rebels, who were initially suspected, explicitly denied any link. The strike came in the same window as the Houthis declaring a naval blockade on **Saudi Arabia**, hitting two Saudi tankers with missiles and drones. **President Trump said the US would hold Iran responsible** and threatened retaliation, without providing evidence of Iranian involvement.
key_points: A drone struck the floating gas storage vessel **Energos Winter** at Egypt's **Damietta port**, and the fire spread to a second ship, the **Gaslog Salem**.
Egypt's government confirmed the blaze was **caused by a drone**, though **no group has claimed responsibility**.
It is the **first known strike on Egyptian soil** since the US and Israel began bombing Iran in February.
Yemen's Houthi rebels **denied involvement**, even as they separately declared a **naval blockade on Saudi Arabia**.
**Trump vowed to hold Iran responsible** and threatened retaliation, raising the risk of the war spreading further.

depth.background: Since February 2026, the **US and Israel have been bombing Iran** and Iran-linked targets across the Middle East, part of a widening conflict that has already pulled in Iraq, Jordan, and Yemen's **Houthi rebels** (an Iran-backed militia that controls much of Yemen and regularly attacks shipping in the Red Sea). Egypt, which controls the **Suez Canal** and hosts major energy infrastructure like the Damietta LNG terminal, had stayed outside the direct fighting until now. The Houthis have separately been escalating attacks on Gulf shipping, this week declaring a blockade on Saudi Arabia — a major escalation that widens the war's economic front even without more countries formally joining the fighting.

stories.title: Haas tests two Toyota-backed Japanese drivers on an old F1 car at Fuji, in a rare scouting look at fresh talent
stories.what_happened: Haas held a **two-day TPC test at Fuji Speedway in Japan on July 28 and 29**, running an older-generation Haas car with two Toyota-backed Japanese drivers, **Sho Tsuboi and Nirei Fukuzumi**, sharing the sessions. The original plan had Tsuboi driving sessions 1 and 4 and Fukuzumi driving 2 and 3, but **rain on the first day forced a change**, with Fukuzumi doing most of the wet-weather running and setting a best lap of **1:18.080** on hard tyres. On day two, in drier conditions, **Tsuboi set a best lap of 1:17.914**, slightly slower than the 1:17.470 he managed in last year's TPC test with an older car. It marked **Fukuzumi's first outing in any grand prix car**, while Tsuboi was making his second F1 test appearance.
key_points: Haas ran a **two-day private test at Fuji Speedway** on **July 28–29** using a **previous-generation F1 car**, under F1's 'Testing of Previous Cars' rules.
Toyota-backed drivers **Sho Tsuboi and Nirei Fukuzumi** shared driving duties across the sessions.
It was **Fukuzumi's first-ever time behind the wheel of a grand prix car**, while Tsuboi was on his second F1 test.
Rain on day one **forced a change of plan**, giving Fukuzumi most of the wet-weather running.
Tsuboi's best lap on day two (**1:17.914**) was close to, but slightly off, his own benchmark from last year's test in an older car.

depth.background: F1 teams are barred from testing their **current-year car** outside a handful of official sessions, to control costs and keep competition fair. But a rule called **'Testing of Previous Cars' (TPC)** lets teams run **older, retired F1 cars** for promotional runs, sponsor days, or — as here — to **scout driver talent** without breaking the current-car ban. Japan has a deep pool of open-wheel talent that rarely gets a shot at F1 machinery, and manufacturers like **Toyota** (which doesn't currently field its own F1 team but backs junior drivers) use these test days to showcase their prospects to F1 teams like Haas.

stories.title: A WWII-era natural experiment finds early-life sugar limits linked to 23% lower dementia risk decades later
stories.what_happened: Researchers analyzing health records for **64,737 people** born in Britain around the end of WWII sugar rationing found that those who spent their **first ~1,000 days of life** (conception to roughly age two) under strict sugar rationing had a **23% lower rate of developing dementia** later in life, compared with people born just after rationing ended in 1953. A slightly shorter exposure — rationing through about age one — was linked to a **21% lower risk**. Among people who did go on to develop dementia, those with less early-life sugar exposure were diagnosed an average of **2.6 years later**. Brain scans of the lower-sugar group also showed **higher total gray matter volume** and **fewer white-matter hyperintensities** — a marker doctors associate with small-vessel brain damage. The study, published July 29, 2026 in the journal *Neurology*, is an association study: it shows a strong statistical link, not direct proof that sugar itself causes the difference.
key_points: People with **very limited sugar** access from conception through age two had a **23% lower rate** of dementia decades later.
Even limited exposure through age one alone was tied to a **21% lower** dementia risk.
For those with less early-life sugar, dementia diagnosis was **delayed by an average of 2.6 years**.
Brains of the low-sugar group showed **more gray matter** and **fewer signs of white-matter damage** on scans.
Researchers used **Britain's WWII-era sugar rationing** (1942–1953) as a real-world before/after comparison across **64,737 people**.

depth.background: During and after World War II, Britain rationed sugar for over a decade, from **1942 to 1953**, sharply limiting how much sugar pregnant women and young children could realistically consume — not by choice, but by national policy. When rationing ended in 1953, sugar consumption jumped almost immediately. That abrupt, nationwide policy shift created an unusual 'natural experiment': researchers could compare the long-term health of people born just before rationing ended (low early-life sugar) against those born just after (higher early-life sugar), without relying on anyone's memory of what they ate as toddlers.

stories.title: India's economy flashes warning signs: trade gap widens, growth slows to a 4-year low, monsoon stays patchy
stories.what_happened: A Bloomberg roundup published July 29, 2026 describes India's economy as sending 'mixed signals' as businesses navigate simultaneous war-related and trade-related shocks. On the trade front, India's **exports grew 15.5% to $40.41 billion** in June — a genuinely strong number, led by electronics and engineering goods — but **imports jumped 31% to a record $70.84 billion**, mainly due to costlier energy imports, widening the trade deficit to **$30.43 billion**, well above the roughly $26.5 billion economists had expected. Separately, broader economic activity tracking showed India's growth slowing to its **weakest pace in more than four years** in July. On the weather side, the monsoon has been volatile: a strong start cut the seasonal rainfall deficit from 40% to 14%, a dry spell pushed it back up to 24%, and a fresh burst of rain between July 21–24 brought it back down to roughly **15%** — still a shortfall, with knock-on risk to crop yields and rural incomes. RBI Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** has publicly named the Iran war and the weak monsoon as the two key risks clouding the outlook.
key_points: India's **merchandise trade deficit widened to $30.43 billion** in June, up from $28.21bn in May, as imports **surged 31%** while exports rose 15.5%.
**Economic activity growth slowed to its weakest pace in more than four years** in July, per Bloomberg's tracking, as Middle East tensions and tariffs raised costs.
**US tariffs** aimed at curbing India's purchases of discounted Russian oil pushed up the cost of imported energy.
The **monsoon rainfall deficit**, which had spiked to 40% earlier in July, has since narrowed to around **15%** after a burst of late-July rain — still leaving farm output at risk.
**RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra** flagged the Iran war and a weak monsoon as the two biggest near-term risks to India's growth.

depth.background: India has spent much of 2026 dealing with the economic fallout of the wider Middle East conflict: higher oil import costs, disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz (the narrow waterway that much of the world's oil passes through), and new US tariffs targeting countries — including India — that kept buying discounted Russian crude oil despite Western sanctions. At the same time, India relies heavily on a good **monsoon season** (June–September) both to water crops directly and to recharge reservoirs that irrigate farms later in the year; a weak monsoon quickly shows up as higher food inflation and slower rural spending.

stories.title: Shane McDermott quits Pakistan's coaching staff to become Afghanistan's fielding coach
stories.what_happened: The **Afghanistan Cricket Board officially confirmed** on July 29, 2026 that Shane McDermott has been appointed the national team's new **Assistant and Fielding Coach**. McDermott previously held the same fielding-coach role with Afghanistan from **January 2024 to July 2025**, before moving to a similar position with the **Pakistan Cricket Board from July 2025**. He resigned from the Pakistan role on **July 18, 2026**, roughly eighteen days before his new Afghanistan appointment was confirmed. McDermott is scheduled to formally **join Afghanistan's coaching staff on August 1, 2026**, in time to prepare the team for its upcoming **five-match ODI series against Ireland**.
key_points: The **Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB)** confirmed Shane McDermott as its new **assistant and fielding coach** on July 29, 2026.
McDermott **resigned from the Pakistan Cricket Board** on July 18, after a year in the same fielding-coach role there.
He previously worked with **Afghanistan from January 2024 to July 2025**, before his stint with Pakistan.
He is set to **join the Afghanistan squad on August 1**, ahead of a **five-match ODI series against Ireland**.
The move is a rare case of a coach switching directly **between two rival national teams** within the same year.

depth.background: International cricket coaching staff — batting, bowling, and fielding coaches — frequently move between national teams, but doing so between two sides that regularly play each other, like Afghanistan and Pakistan, is unusual and can draw scrutiny over potential conflicts of interest, since the coach knows a rival team's methods and personnel intimately. Fielding coaches specifically work on catching, ground fielding, and athleticism — an area increasingly seen as a difference-maker in modern limited-overs cricket.

stories.title: France's Bordeaux-area wildfires stabilize as 60,000 evacuees are cleared to go home — but flare-ups continue
stories.what_happened: French authorities said the wildfires near Bordeaux have **stabilized**, allowing roughly **60,000 evacuees from three towns** just outside the city to return home. That's a meaningful de-escalation from days earlier, when nearly **4,000 more people** had to be evacuated as a heat spike threatened firefighters' fragile hold on the blaze. However, the Gironde prefecture also warned that **several fires have reignited inside areas that had already burned**, especially around Lège-Cap-Ferret/Grand Crohot and Marcheprime — a reminder that dry, scorched land can catch fire again even after the main blaze is contained. Around **224,000 people** have been evacuated in total since the fires began, and firefighters are bracing for another heatwave that forecasters say could again test containment lines.
key_points: Authorities say the wildfires burning in France's **Gironde region**, near Bordeaux, have **'stabilized'** after weeks of explosive growth.
Around **60,000 people** from three towns a few miles from Bordeaux are now being allowed back into their homes.
The fires have forced roughly **224,000 evacuations in total** since they began — one of France's biggest peacetime evacuation efforts.
New fires have **reignited inside already-burned areas**, particularly around Lège/Grand Crohot and Marcheprime, showing the danger isn't over.
A fresh **heatwave** is forecast to return, which could threaten the fragile containment firefighters have achieved.

depth.background: In late July, a wildfire broke out in France's Gironde department and grew explosively, at one point generating its own lightning — a rare 'fire thunderstorm' effect called pyrocumulonimbus that had never been documented in France before. At its peak the fire had burned more than **42,000 hectares** and forced the evacuation of roughly **220,000 people**, including a full evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula. **Bordeaux city itself, a UNESCO World Heritage site of 270,000 residents, was never evacuated**, but many surrounding towns were emptied for days.

thread.previously: We reported France evacuating 4,000 more people as a heat spike threatened the fragile Bordeaux wildfire containment.
thread.changed: The fire has now stabilized enough that 60,000 of the roughly 224,000 total evacuees are being allowed home, though flare-ups continue in already-burned areas and a new heatwave is forecast.

stories.title: Landslides shut 150+ roads in Himachal Pradesh, strand pilgrims on the Yamunotri highway in Uttarakhand
stories.what_happened: As of **July 29**, **152 roads** are shut across Himachal Pradesh due to landslides and flash floods — the worst-hit district is **Mandi with 57 closures**, followed by Chamba (33), Kullu (31) and Shimla (14). The damage has also knocked out **68 water-supply schemes and 72 power transformers**. Palampur recorded **133mm of rain in just 24 hours**, prompting India's weather office to issue an **orange alert** (meaning be prepared, significant weather expected) for four districts through July 30. Next door in Uttarakhand, landslides have blocked **120 roads, including three national highways**, and around **100 pilgrims were stranded** on a washed-out stretch of the Yamunotri National Highway — part of the Char Dham pilgrimage route — for two days before being escorted across.
key_points: **152 roads** are shut across Himachal Pradesh after heavy rain triggered landslides and flash floods.
**57 of those closures are in Mandi district** alone; 68 water-supply schemes and 72 power transformers are also down.
Palampur recorded **133mm of rain in 24 hours**; IMD has issued an **orange alert** for four districts.
In Uttarakhand, landslides blocked **120 roads including three national highways**, stranding about **100 pilgrims** on the Yamunotri route for two days.

depth.background: Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand are Himalayan states whose narrow mountain roads are especially prone to landslides during India's **monsoon season** (roughly June to September), when saturated hillsides give way easily. Both states are also major pilgrimage corridors — Uttarakhand's **Char Dham** route, including Yamunotri, draws hundreds of thousands of pilgrims each monsoon despite the known risks, and road blockages there regularly strand travelers for days. This year's monsoon has already caused significant damage further east in **Assam**, so this is a second, separate flood/landslide emergency unfolding at the same time in the north.

stories.title: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi jumps 230 places in ICC T20I rankings after Zimbabwe series MVP show
stories.what_happened: Following India's three-match T20I series in Harare, Zimbabwe, **15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** jumped **230 places** in the ICC men's T20I batting rankings to a career-best **48th**. He was named **Player of the Series** after scoring **151 runs at an average of 50.33**, including a **19-ball fifty** and an **81 off 49 balls** in the decider. The achievement makes him the **first player in men's T20I history to score more than one half-century before turning 16**. The same ICC rankings update also saw West Indies pacers **Justin Greaves** (up 21 places to a career-high 48th in Test bowling) and **Jayden Seales** (up to 24th) rise sharply, following their five-wicket hauls against Pakistan.
key_points: Sooryavanshi jumped **230 places** to a career-best **48th** in the ICC men's T20I batting rankings.
He was named **Player of the Series** after scoring **151 runs at an average of 50.33** in Zimbabwe.
His knocks included a **19-ball fifty** and an **81 off 49 balls** in the series decider.
He's the **first player in men's T20I history** to score more than one half-century before turning 16.

depth.background: **Vaibhav Sooryavanshi** has been one of Indian cricket's most closely watched teenage prospects, drawing attention for scoring rapid, aggressive innings well beyond his age at domestic level before making his senior India T20I debut. The **ICC player rankings** are a widely-used, points-based system that ranks international cricketers on recent form and match performance — a jump of over 200 places in one series is extremely rare and signals a major statistical breakout. This series in Zimbabwe was one of his first extended runs of matches for the senior India team.

stories.title: West Indies crush Pakistan by 90 runs in first Test — Babar's team suffers a fourth straight Test loss
stories.what_happened: West Indies beat Pakistan by **90 runs** in the first Test at the **Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba, Trinidad**, bowling Pakistan out for just **120** in the fourth innings while defending a target of 211. Fast bowler **Jayden Seales** took a five-wicket haul in the second innings, backed by **Justin Greaves**, who claimed career-best match figures including **7/39** — a total of **40 wickets fell in the match**, reflecting seam-friendly conditions throughout. It is Pakistan's **fourth straight Test loss** and their **eighth consecutive defeat away from home**, extending a brutal run under returning captain **Babar Azam**. Pakistan's chief selector, former captain **Misbah-ul-Haq**, said publicly that 'the captain has to take responsibility' for the defeat. The two-match series concludes with the second Test starting **August 2** at Queen's Park Oval, Port of Spain.
key_points: West Indies bowled Pakistan out for **120** to win the first Test by **90 runs** in Tarouba, Trinidad.
**Jayden Seales** took a five-wicket haul; **Justin Greaves** claimed career-best figures of **7/39**.
It's Pakistan's **fourth consecutive Test defeat** and eighth straight loss away from home.
Chief selector **Misbah-ul-Haq** said captain **Babar Azam** 'has to take responsibility' for the result.
The second and final Test starts **August 2** at Queen's Park Oval.

depth.background: **Babar Azam** returned as Pakistan's Test captain after **Shan Masood** was sacked from the role earlier this year, following a run of poor results. Pakistan has struggled badly playing Test cricket away from home in recent years, a pattern this result extends. **West Indies**, meanwhile, have been rebuilding a Test side that fell to historic lows earlier in the decade, and a dominant, seam-friendly win at home is a meaningful marker of progress for their bowling attack.

stories.title: Mercedes told points leader Antonelli 'don't waste time racing' Norris — and it may have cost him the Hungarian GP win
stories.what_happened: Newly surfaced radio transcripts from the **Hungarian Grand Prix** show Mercedes race engineer **Peter Bonnington** telling leader Antonelli, with two laps remaining, **'Norris at 1.8, we don't want to waste time racing him'** — effectively instructing Antonelli not to fight for the position on his older tyres. Norris then attacked into **Turn 1**, ran wide under pressure, and Antonelli briefly re-passed him — but Norris won the position back moments later and went on to take the win. Antonelli has since said a **'safety concern'** was behind Mercedes' call to stand down rather than defend hard. Norris says the title fight is **'alive'**, pointing to Mercedes' in-race decision-making as Antonelli's biggest weakness heading into the second half of the season.
key_points: Radio transcripts show Mercedes engineer **Peter Bonnington** telling Antonelli **'we don't want to waste time racing'** Norris with two laps left.
Antonelli was told **not to defend the lead** from Norris on older tyres.
**Norris lunged** at Turn 1, ran wide, and Antonelli briefly re-passed — but Norris won moments later anyway.
Antonelli has since cited a **'safety concern'** behind Mercedes' call; Norris says the **title fight is 'alive'**.

depth.background: **Kimi Antonelli** leads the F1 drivers' championship for Mercedes, with **Lando Norris** and McLaren his closest rival — a title fight that has swung on strategy calls and late-race incidents all season. At the **Hungarian Grand Prix**, Antonelli was leading in the closing laps but running on older, more worn tyres than Norris, who had made a later pit stop. Team radio — the constant communication between driver and engineers during a race — often reveals in-the-moment strategic calls that only become public well after the race, once broadcasters or journalists obtain the untelevised portions.

stories.title: F1 points leader Kimi Antonelli sued by former manager over 2025 contract termination
stories.what_happened: Giovanni Minardi has filed a lawsuit against **Kimi Antonelli**, the current Mercedes driver leading the F1 drivers' championship, in a court in **Bologna, Italy**. Minardi discovered Antonelli at a summer camp in **2014** and signed him to a management deal, but says the relationship was abruptly and wrongfully terminated in **2025** — the same year Antonelli graduated to a full-time Mercedes F1 seat. He is seeking **six-figure damages** for breach of contract, according to multiple Italian and F1 outlets. The dispute reportedly simmered privately for about a year before becoming public. **Toto Wolff** and Mercedes junior-programme chief Gwen Lagrue could be called to testify given their role in Antonelli's later career.
key_points: **Giovanni Minardi**, son of the old Minardi F1 team's founder, is suing championship leader **Kimi Antonelli** in a Bologna court.
Minardi discovered and signed Antonelli in **2014** after spotting him at a summer camp.
The management relationship ended in **2025**, the same year Antonelli made his F1 debut.
Minardi is seeking **six-figure compensation** for what he calls a wrongful termination.
**Toto Wolff** and Mercedes' junior-programme chief could be called as witnesses.

depth.background: Long before a driver reaches Formula 1, a web of junior-career managers, academies and sponsors typically shapes (and profits from) their rise — these management contracts can run for years and are a normal, if rarely public, part of how F1 talent gets funded and guided. **Giovanni Minardi** runs Minardi Management, unrelated to the old Minardi F1 team beyond his father's name, and has a track record of spotting young Italian talent. He signed **Kimi Antonelli** as a child in 2014, well before Mercedes took over developing him as a junior-program prospect who eventually graduated to a race seat in 2025.

stories.title: China puts a quiet coast-guard 'squeeze' on the waters east of Taiwan
stories.what_happened: Throughout June and July, China's Maritime Safety Administration and its coast guard staged multiple patrols and what Beijing called 'special maritime law enforcement operations' in the waters east of Taiwan. Analysts say this is the first time China has moved these patrols east of the island in such quick succession — previously, Chinese coast-guard activity concentrated near Taiwan's outlying islands close to the mainland, like Kinmen, rather than the open ocean facing the Pacific. Because the ships involved are technically law-enforcement rather than navy vessels, Beijing can frame the patrols as **routine policing** rather than military aggression, making a diplomatic or military response harder to justify. In response, the US and Taiwan's coast guards have started operating together at sea; the American Institute in Taiwan — the US's unofficial embassy on the island — posted a photo Tuesday showing the two coast guards side by side, saying they were coordinating on search-and-rescue, disaster relief and maritime law enforcement.
key_points: China's coast guard and civilian ships have run repeated patrols in waters **east of Taiwan** through June and July — the first time patrols have moved east this fast.
Analysts say the pattern looks like a **rehearsal for a blockade-style 'quarantine'** that could cut Taiwan off from trade without firing a shot.
Unlike four years of sporadic military jet and warship drills, this is framed by Beijing as **routine law enforcement**, making objections harder.
The **US and Taiwan coast guards** have started operating side-by-side in response, with the American Institute in Taiwan publicly posting a photo of the joint patrol.

depth.background: China claims self-ruled **Taiwan** as its own territory and has spent years pressuring it, mostly through military jets crossing into Taiwan's air defense zone and naval drills that circle the island. Those actions are provocative but happen in bursts, and other countries can point to them as clear military intimidation. A coast-guard patrol is different: it looks like ordinary policing, but China's coast guard operates under Beijing's control and has been used before to assert control over disputed waters, most notably in the **South China Sea**. Taiwan's economy depends heavily on shipping — it imports nearly all its energy and much of its food by sea — so any credible threat to its sea lanes is taken seriously in Taipei and Washington.

stories.title: NASA's Psyche spacecraft releases stunning time-lapse video from its Mars flyby en route to a metal asteroid
stories.what_happened: In May 2026, the Psyche spacecraft swung past Mars, using the planet's gravity in a maneuver called a **gravity assist** to gain speed and bend its path toward the asteroid belt without burning extra fuel. It passed as close as **4,500 km (2,800 miles)** above the Martian surface, and in the process its cameras — originally built to study a metal asteroid, not Mars — captured detailed images of craters, windblown dust patterns, the **south polar ice cap**, and the large double-ringed Huygens crater. NASA's science team spent the following weeks processing the raw images into a time-lapse video, which it released publicly this week alongside the flyby data. The maneuver sped the spacecraft up from about **45,600 mph to 52,200 mph** relative to the Sun. Psyche is now on course to arrive at asteroid 16 Psyche in **2029**, when it will begin mapping the object's surface and testing whether it really is an exposed planetary core.
key_points: Psyche used Mars's gravity to slingshot itself toward asteroid 16 Psyche, speeding up from **45,600 mph to 52,200 mph** relative to the Sun
The spacecraft flew as close as **4,500 km** above the Martian surface
NASA released a new time-lapse video and detailed images this week, including Mars's south polar ice cap and the giant Huygens crater
The mission's ultimate target, asteroid Psyche, is believed to be the exposed **metal core of a failed baby planet**
Psyche launched in **October 2023** and will reach the asteroid in **2029**

depth.background: Most asteroids are rock or ice, but 16 Psyche — a roughly 140-mile-wide object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter — appears to be made largely of nickel and iron, the same metal that makes up Earth's core. Scientists think it may be the leftover core of an early **planetesimal**, a building block of a planet that got stripped of its outer rock layers by violent collisions billions of years ago. NASA launched the **Psyche spacecraft** in October 2023 specifically to study this object up close — the first mission ever aimed at a metal world. Studying it could reveal what the deep interior of a planet like Earth actually looks like, since we can never directly drill down to our own core.

stories.title: Lok Sabha extends the 'One Nation, One Election' committee's deadline to the Monsoon Session's final week
stories.what_happened: The Lok Sabha voted to **extend the JPC's working deadline again**, pushing it to the **first day of the last week of the ongoing 2026 Monsoon Session**. JPC chairman **P.P. Chaudhary** moved the extension resolution, and the House passed it on a **voice vote** rather than a recorded division. The extension gives the committee more time to continue consulting stakeholders — political parties, state governments, legal experts and the public — across the country before finalizing its position. Sources close to the committee suggest it may seek a **further extension** given how complex and contested the underlying constitutional questions are, meaning a final report is now expected only in the **Winter Session** of Parliament.
key_points: The Lok Sabha (India's lower house of Parliament) approved another extension for the **41-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** studying the 'One Nation, One Election' bills.
The JPC is examining the **Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill**, which would let Lok Sabha, state assembly and eventually local body elections happen **on a single common schedule**.
The extension, moved by JPC chairman **P.P. Chaudhary**, was passed by a **voice vote** — no formal division was called.
The committee's new deadline is the **first day of the last week of the 2026 Monsoon Session**, but it may seek yet another extension given the scale of the consultations.
The JPC is meant to submit a **final report during the Winter Session** after consulting stakeholders across the country.

depth.background: 'One Nation, One Election' is a long-standing proposal, championed by the Modi government, to synchronize India's staggered election calendar — where different states currently vote for their assemblies at different times — into a single nationwide cycle held alongside Lok Sabha elections. Supporters argue it would cut the cost and administrative strain of near-constant campaigning; critics argue it could weaken state-level accountability. The **Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill**, which would enable the change, was referred to a specially formed **41-member Joint Parliamentary Committee** for detailed scrutiny because it touches the structure of India's federal democracy.

stories.title: Sri Lanka Women win their first bilateral ODI series over Pakistan in 24 years
stories.what_happened: In the series-deciding 3rd ODI at Sooriyawewa, Hambantota, on **July 28**, Sri Lanka Women beat Pakistan Women by **8 wickets** with 76 balls to spare to win the series 2-1. Seamer Chethana Vimukthi removed three of Pakistan's top-order batters cheaply in her second over, and Pakistan were eventually bowled out for **187** despite useful innings from Gull Feroza (40) and captain Fatima Sana (41). Sri Lanka chased the target down comfortably, reaching 191/2, with half-centuries from Harshitha Samarawickrama (71 not out) and Hasini Perera (50 not out). **Chamari Athapaththu** was named Player of the Match for scoring 52 off 38 balls and taking 3 wickets for 27 runs, while Samarawickrama's 173 series runs earned her Player of the Series.
key_points: Sri Lanka Women won the series decider by **8 wickets** with 76 balls to spare
It's their **first bilateral ODI series win over Pakistan in 24 years**
**Chethana Vimukthi** ripped through Pakistan's top order early, taking 3 wickets cheaply
**Chamari Athapaththu** was Player of the Match (52 off 38, plus 3/27); Samarawickrama was Player of the Series

depth.background: The three-match series was part of the **ICC Women's Championship**, the qualification pathway to the next Women's ODI World Cup, so every match carries points toward World Cup qualification. Pakistan had taken a 1-0 lead in the first match before Sri Lanka leveled the series in the second.

stories.title: Iran fires ballistic missiles directly at a US base in Jordan — its first direct strike since Trump paused the bombing
stories.what_happened: On Tuesday evening, the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles at a **US military base in Jordan** in what US Central Command called an 'attempted surprise attack.' Every missile was **shot down before reaching its target**, and no American casualties were reported. The strike came after Iran-aligned militias fired **more than 30 drones** at US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure over the preceding three days, prompting the US and Saudi Arabia to jointly strike militia sites inside Iraq in response. Hours after the missile attack, Brent crude — the global oil price benchmark — jumped **more than 7% to $90.66 a barrel**. President Trump told Fox News that Iran would 'get a beating' for the attempt. Separately, Israel's military accused Hezbollah of attacking an engineering vehicle in Lebanon, calling it a 'blatant violation' of their ceasefire.
key_points: Iran's **Revolutionary Guard (IRGC)** fired multiple ballistic missiles at a US military base in **Jordan**; US Central Command says **all were intercepted**.
The attack followed **more than 30 IRGC-directed drone strikes** on US troops and Saudi oil facilities over the prior **72 hours**.
**Brent crude jumped over 7% to $90.66 a barrel**, its sharpest spike of the year, on fears of a wider war.
President Trump told Fox News Iran is **'going to get a beating'**, signaling a tougher US response is coming.
Israel separately accused **Hezbollah** of breaking the Lebanon ceasefire the same day, opening a second front of tension.

depth.background: Iran and Israel have been in an on-and-off shooting war for much of this year, with the **US** backing Israel and occasionally striking Iranian-linked targets directly. Trump had paused direct American strikes on Iran in recent weeks to give diplomacy a chance, and Tehran had briefly held back its own retaliatory attacks. The **IRGC** is Iran's elite military force, separate from its regular army, and answers directly to the Supreme Leader rather than the elected government — it runs Iran's missile and proxy-militia programs across the Middle East.

stories.title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East, all intercepted — oil jumps 5%
stories.what_happened: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched what US officials called an **"attempted surprise attack"** on American forces stationed in the Middle East at around 5:45pm ET on Tuesday, July 28. Initial estimates put the number of missiles fired at **no more than four**; CENTCOM says every one of them was intercepted before reaching its target, and no injuries have been reported. The attack landed hours after Trump and Netanyahu met at the White House specifically to discuss Iran policy — with Netanyahu pushing for continued military pressure and Trump favoring the negotiated track his administration has been running. Oil traders read the strike as a sign the ceasefire-adjacent calm of the past few days is fraying: **Brent crude rose about 1.1% to $83 a barrel and WTI jumped over 4%**, clawing back Monday's decline that had come on hopes the US was standing down.
key_points: Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched **up to four ballistic missiles** at US forces around 5:45pm ET
US Central Command says **all the missiles were intercepted**, with no reported casualties
Brent crude jumped roughly **5% to about $83 a barrel**, reversing Monday's price drop
The attack came just hours after **Trump and Netanyahu discussed Iran** at the White House
Shipping through the **Strait of Hormuz** has been largely blocked by Iran since February 28

depth.background: The US and Israel launched an air war against Iran in late February 2026, and fighting has flared on and off since, centered on the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that roughly a **fifth of the world's oil** passes through. Iran has used the threat of blocking the strait as its main point of leverage, while the US has alternated between striking Iranian targets and pursuing a negotiated de-escalation. On Monday, Washington had paused plans to escalate further, and Tuesday's White House meeting between Trump and Netanyahu was explicitly billed as a fork in the road: keep pressing Iran militarily, or stick with diplomacy.

thread.previously: We reported that Netanyahu and Trump were meeting at the White House on July 28 specifically to hash out whether to keep pressing Iran militarily or stick with the negotiated track — a fork in the road for the region.
thread.changed: Hours after that meeting, Iran actually launched a ballistic-missile attack on US forces, which was fully intercepted — turning the meeting's abstract choice into an immediate, live test of which path the US takes next.
