stories.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear pleas on police 'excesses' against NEET protesters, but rejects an urgent listing
stories.what_happened: A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant is hearing two petitions today alleging that Delhi Police used disproportionate force — tear gas, lathi charges and other measures — against students protesting the NEET paper-leak issue on July 20. The court had initially declined a request for an urgent, out-of-turn hearing, with the Chief Justice reportedly telling the petitioners' lawyer not to waste the court's time, but agreed the matter would be taken up in the ordinary course today. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, argued the police response amounted to 'police excess... going against students.'
key_points: CJI Surya Kant's bench will hear two pleas on the July 20 Delhi police crackdown today
Court had earlier declined to list the matter urgently, telling lawyers 'please don't waste our time'
Petitions allege tear gas and lathi-charge were used against NEET paper-leak protesters
Case is separate from the government's talks with protest leaders and the new anti-paper-leak bill

depth.background: Student protests over an alleged leak in this year's NEET-UG medical entrance exam have been building for weeks under the banner of the 'Cockroach Janta Party,' culminating in a 'Chalo Sansad' march toward Parliament on July 20 that Delhi Police broke up with tear gas and lathi charges — injuring, by some accounts, dozens of protesters and police alike. One young woman critically hurt in that crackdown was taken off ventilator support and is now stable, as we reported yesterday. Two separate petitions were then filed asking the Supreme Court to examine whether the police used excessive force.

stories.title: Government holds its first direct talks with NEET protest leaders — but makes no commitments
stories.what_happened: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation at his residence — the first direct negotiation between the government and protest leaders since the crackdown. The delegation submitted a written memorandum and appealed to protesters to end their sit-in. Nadda said he would raise their concerns 'at the appropriate level' but offered no firm commitments. CJP leaders say the protest continues until remaining demands — ₹1 crore compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide amid the scandal, and the release of hospitalized activist Sonam Wangchuk — are met.
key_points: Union Health Minister JP Nadda met a CJP delegation for the first negotiation since the Chalo Sansad crackdown
The group submitted a written memorandum and asked protesters to end their sit-in
CJP says no real commitments were made; the protest continues
Remaining demands: ₹1 crore compensation for NEET-related suicide victims and activist Sonam Wangchuk's release from hospital

depth.background: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has led a weeks-long protest movement over alleged irregularities in India's NEET medical entrance exam, including a paper-leak scandal. Protesters tried to march on Parliament in a 'Chalo Sansad' demonstration; police used a lathi charge to disperse the crowd, critically injuring a woman who was later taken off ventilator support — a story we've covered. Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, one of the protesters' original targets, has since resigned and been replaced by Pralhad Joshi.

stories.title: Netanyahu heads to the White House for a tense Trump meeting, with Iran splitting the two leaders
stories.what_happened: Netanyahu departs for Washington today ahead of a Tuesday meeting with Trump, his sixth Oval Office sit-down since Trump's return to office and his first since the Iran war escalated. The two leaders are expected to clash over next steps on Iran: Netanyahu is pushing for a renewed round of military strikes, while **Trump** — who ordered a halt to two weeks of nightly US bombing raids on Iran last week — is said to prefer giving diplomacy more room. Ahead of the trip, Netanyahu has made conciliatory gestures on Gaza and Lebanon that Israeli commentators read as an attempt to arrive in Washington looking like a cooperative partner rather than a source of friction. While in Washington, Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham**, a longtime Israel ally in Congress. The meeting lands at a delicate moment: the fragile US-Iran halt in hostilities is only days old, and how the two leaders align — or don't — could determine whether it holds.
key_points: Netanyahu meets Trump at the White House on **Tuesday**, his first visit since the Iran war began.
It will be his **sixth** Oval Office meeting with Trump in a year and a half — more than any other world leader.
Iran is the central divide: Netanyahu wants **renewed military action**, Trump leans toward **diplomacy**.
The visit comes days after the US paused its **two weeks of nightly airstrikes** on Iran.
Netanyahu will also attend the funeral of **Senator Lindsey Graham** while in Washington.

depth.background: Since the Iran conflict escalated, the US and Israel have coordinated closely but not always agreed on how far to push militarily. The US carried out nightly strikes on Iran for two weeks before pausing them last week as **Trump** signaled he wants room for diplomacy. Netanyahu has now visited the Trump White House **five times before** this trip, reflecting how central the US alliance is to Israel's wartime strategy — but this is his first visit since the Iran war intensified.

stories.title: China's Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the largest open-weight AI model ever built
stories.what_happened: Beijing-based Moonshot AI released the open weights for **Kimi K3**, a **2.8-trillion-parameter** AI model, making it downloadable for free roughly **a day earlier** than the company's own July 27 target. The model uses a 'sparse mixture-of-experts' design, meaning it only activates a small slice of its total parameters for any given task, which keeps inference costs down compared to a dense model of the same size. It supports a **1-million-token context window**, letting it process entire codebases or large document sets in a single pass. On independent benchmarks, K3 ranked behind only Anthropic's and OpenAI's top models on general intelligence, while beating other rivals, including Anthropic's Opus-tier model, on coding and agentic tasks specifically. Moonshot priced API access at **$3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens** — the highest of any Chinese lab, but still roughly half the cost of Anthropic's premium model for comparable work.
key_points: Kimi K3 has **2.8 trillion parameters**, making it the largest open-weight AI model released to date.
Moonshot AI shipped the free download **a day early**, at roughly 7:30pm EDT on July 26.
It only activates a fraction of its parameters per request (a 'mixture-of-experts' design), keeping running costs down despite its size.
It ranks **fourth overall** on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, just behind Claude and GPT's top models but ahead of several others.
Moonshot is charging **roughly half** what Anthropic charges for its priciest model, undercutting Western rivals on price.

depth.background: 'Open-weight' models are AI systems whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and run, unlike 'closed' models such as those from OpenAI or Anthropic, which are only accessible through a paid API. Chinese AI labs, including Moonshot AI, have leaned into open-weight releases partly because **U.S. export controls limit their access to the most advanced computer chips**, making it harder to compete purely on raw compute — so they compete on giving the model away and letting the ecosystem build on it instead. Moonshot's prior model, Kimi K2.6, was already a well-regarded open-weight system; K3 is a major step up in scale.

stories.title: Gunmen kill at least 30 in a midnight raid on Naridon village in Kaduna State
stories.what_happened: At around 11 pm on Sunday, July 26, gunmen invaded Naridon village in Kauru Local Government Area of Kaduna State, firing indiscriminately at residents before setting houses and shops ablaze. At least **30 people were killed, including 8 children**, and several more were injured; recovery teams warned the toll could climb further. The attackers reportedly operated for hours without being confronted. Residents said military units stationed roughly two kilometres away in nearby Kamaru and Ungwan Magaji did not arrive in time to stop the killing, and that only a single soldier and four Mobile Police officers were deployed to the community afterward. The Kaduna state government has condemned the attack and ordered security agencies to hunt down those responsible.
key_points: Gunmen attacked Naridon village around **11 pm on Sunday**, shooting residents and torching homes.
At least **30 people are dead, including 8 children**, with search teams fearing the toll could rise.
Nearby military posts were just **2 kilometres away** but reportedly did not respond during the hours-long attack.
Only **one soldier and four police officers** were stationed in the village after the killings.
The state government has ordered a **manhunt** and called the attack 'barbaric'.

depth.background: Naridon sits on the border between Kaduna and Plateau states, a stretch of central Nigeria known as the 'Middle Belt' where farming communities (mostly Christian) and herding communities (mostly Muslim Fulani) have clashed for years over land and water, a conflict often called the **Southern Kaduna crisis**. Armed groups — sometimes described as bandits, sometimes as militias — have repeatedly raided villages here with little warning and, residents say, little protection. Kaduna's state government has struggled for years to contain the violence despite repeated pledges of tougher security.

stories.title: F1's summer-break report card: Antonelli's rookie masterclass, and a rough half-season for Verstappen
stories.what_happened: With Formula 1 entering its summer break after the Hungarian Grand Prix, mid-season assessments graded every team's performance under this year's new technical rules. Mercedes' 19-year-old rookie **Kimi Antonelli** has been the story of the season, winning six races and taking podiums in all but two starts to become the youngest driver ever to lead the championship at this stage. Mercedes as a team holds a commanding **78-point lead** over Ferrari in the constructors' standings. The bigger shock is at Red Bull, where four-time champion Max Verstappen sits 7th in the drivers' standings without a single win — reports point to Red Bull's car struggling with electrical deployment and its adaptation to the new active-aerodynamics rules, leaving Verstappen relying on pure driving skill to stay competitive. McLaren, which set the pace for much of last season, has also fallen short on both speed and reliability, with Lando Norris trailing Antonelli by 91 points.
key_points: Rookie **Kimi Antonelli**, 19, leads the drivers' championship at the summer break — the **youngest driver ever** to lead the standings, with **six wins** and podiums in all but two races.
**Mercedes** leads the constructors' championship by a wide margin, up **78 points** on second-placed Ferrari at the break.
**Max Verstappen sits 7th** in the standings with **zero wins** so far — a shock given his recent dominance — with Red Bull's new-rules car reportedly lagging Mercedes and Ferrari.
**McLaren**, last year's benchmark team, has lacked both pace and reliability to keep up, leaving Lando Norris **91 points** behind Antonelli.
The grades come at F1's annual **summer break**, the multi-week pause when teams and press traditionally take stock of the season so far.

depth.background: F1 introduced a major overhaul of its technical rules for the 2026 season — new engines and aerodynamics — the biggest regulatory shake-up since 2022, which reshuffled the competitive order and made this year's midpoint report card unusually consequential. The sport's summer break sits roughly at the season's halfway point and gives teams and commentators a natural pause to assess who has adapted best to the new rules before the run to the championship resumes.
